name: Addons
description: Other mods that add optional content when installed with Aetherhaven
text: Addons Aetherhaven works on its own. Some Hexvane (and partner) mods can optionally plug in when both are installed: extra villagers, shops, quest board jobs, gift tastes, and journal pages. Nothing here is required to run Aetherhaven. Install an addon only if you want that pack’s town content. Known integrations Mod What you get with Aetherhaven ----- ------------------------------- Mechanic villager Rivet Cogsworth , mechanics shop, rescue quest, shop stock Fisherman Reed Castwell , fishing shop, gear/fish shop spots, treasure extras Each overview page explains how to unlock that content. Villager detail pages cover quests, friendship, schedules, and gifts—same style as the Town Journal. For modders Want your mod to appear here? See under For developers.

name: Cozy Tales Fishing
description: Optional Aetherhaven integration from Cozy Tales Fishing
text: Cozy Tales: Fishing Cozy Tales: Fishing is a relaxed fishing pack (rods, bobbers, aquariums, fishing journal). It works alone. With Aetherhaven installed alongside it, you get extra town content. What you get with both mods - Reed Castwell , a castaway fisherman with dialogue and tips - A fishing shop you help establish (blueprint → plot crafting bench → shop prefab) - Shop stock and prices for fishing gear - Extra rewards from sunken treasure (gold coins and the occasional jewelry) Aetherhaven is not required for fishing. Install both only if you want the integration. How to unlock Reed 1. Install Cozy Tales: Fishing and Aetherhaven . 2. Finish Vex's market stall so Reed can appear in the inn visitor pool. 3. Talk to Reed at the inn, accept the fishing shop quest, learn the blueprint at the plot crafting bench, and build the shop. 4. Optionally build Reed a house the same way as other residents. Full quest steps, schedule, and gift tastes: . Related Aetherhaven systems - - - (treasure can drop unidentified pieces)

name: Machinaria
description: Optional Aetherhaven integration from the Machinaria scrapyard mod
text: Machinaria Machinaria adds a rusty scrapyard fragment and crafting gadgets. It also ships an optional Aetherhaven integration —you do not need Machinaria for Aetherhaven, and you do not need Aetherhaven for Machinaria’s core loop. What you get with both mods - Rivet Cogsworth , a robot mechanic freed from rust with black oil - Inn unlock after the rescue, then shop and house quests - A mechanics shop selling metal and gear from the Rusted Expanse (vanilla metal sets plus Machinaria blocks) - Quest board fetch jobs and a journal guide page for Rivet How to unlock Rivet 1. Install Machinaria and Aetherhaven on the same world or server. 2. In the Rusted Expanse, find a rusty robot, break it for the block, and throw it into oil. 3. Talk with Rivet when they wake, then meet them at the inn. 4. Accept shop and house quests from Rivet at the inn, and build the mechanics shop / house as usual. Full quest steps, schedule, and gift tastes: . Related Aetherhaven systems Shop spots and NPC restock work the same as for Vex and other workers—see . Plot tokens and blueprints use the same tools as the rest of town—see .

name: Crossmod integration
description: How other mods add villagers, buildings, dialogue, and more via asset packs
text: Crossmod integration with Aetherhaven This guide explains how another mod can add villagers, buildings, dialogue, quests, quest board pools, shop stock, prices, and field-rescue talk using assets (and a little Java when you need custom UI or conditions). Aetherhaven scans every registered asset pack for files under Server/Aetherhaven/ . Your mod should ship an asset pack ( IncludesAssetPack: true ) and list Aetherhaven as an optional or hard dependency so it loads in a sensible order. Manifest Use a hard Dependencies entry if your mod cannot run without Aetherhaven. Folder map Place content under your pack root: Path Purpose ------------------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------- Server/Aetherhaven/Villagers/ Villager gameplay defs (dialogue trees, gifts, schedules, inn pool) Server/Aetherhaven/VillagerGiftPatches/ Append gift loves/likes/dislikes onto an existing villager Server/Aetherhaven/VillagerSchedules/ Weekly schedules by NPC role id Server/Aetherhaven/ScheduleLocations/ Custom schedule location symbols mapped to buildings Server/Aetherhaven/VillagerSchedulePatches/ Add, replace, or remove schedule times on existing roles Server/Aetherhaven/GuideTopics/ Journal guide markdown pages ( <locale /<topicId .md ) Server/Aetherhaven/GuidePatches/ Append guide hub sub-topics (e.g. under villagers ) Server/Aetherhaven/NpcRoles/ Engine NPC roles (only loaded when Aetherhaven is present) Server/Aetherhaven/NpcModels/ Optional NPC models for those roles (AH-gated) Server/Aetherhaven/Dialogue/ Full dialogue trees (same id overrides earlier packs) Server/Aetherhaven/DialoguePatches/ Inject choices/nodes into an existing tree Server/Aetherhaven/Quests/ Story / housing quests Server/Aetherhaven/QuestBoardExtensions/ Extra quest board fetch/hunt/raid entries Server/Aetherhaven/Buildings/ Construction definitions Server/Aetherhaven/Festivals/ Festival definitions swapped onto the festival square Server/Aetherhaven/ShopPrices/ Gold prices for shop spots Server/Aetherhaven/ShopLoot/ Shop spot loot tables (append or replace) Server/Aetherhaven/Townsfolk/ Townsfolk character pool Server/Aetherhaven/Personalities/ Personality traits Server/Prefabs/ Building prefabs referenced by constructions Server/Languages/en-US/ English lang keys Same content id from a later pack replaces an earlier pack for whole-file catalogs (villagers, dialogue trees, quests, buildings). Prices, loot, quest board pools, dialogue patches, gift patches, and schedule patches merge as described below. Villagers and NPC roles Crossmod villagers should put engine NPC roles under Server/Aetherhaven/NpcRoles/ , not under Server/NPC/Roles/ . Hytale only auto-loads Server/NPC/Roles/ ; Aetherhaven scans NpcRoles after its dialogue action, attitude groups, and Aetherhaven Human exist. If Aetherhaven is missing, those role files are ignored. 1. Add role JSON under Server/Aetherhaven/NpcRoles/ (role id = filename without .json ). Interact should open Aetherhaven dialogue ( OpenAetherhavenDialogue ), same pattern as Aetherhaven’s own roles. Optional component files can live under NpcRoles/.../Components/ (loaded before spawnable roles). 2. Optional appearance models under Server/Aetherhaven/NpcModels/ (model id = filename). You may still parent models to Aetherhaven Human or reuse Aetherhaven villager models that already ship with Aetherhaven under Server/Models/ . 3. Add a villager definition under Server/Aetherhaven/Villagers/ with matching npcRoleId , residentTreeId / visitorTreeId , gifts, schedule bindings, and so on. 4. For a shop worker who starts in the inn pool: set innPoolEligible , visitorBindingKind (e.g. visitor angler ), workConstructionId to your shop building id (not plot house ), and dialogueVillagerKind (resident kind after promotion, e.g. angler ). Use countsAsConstructionId: ["plot house"] on the building when it should also offer a resident bed; Aetherhaven uses house residency separately from workplace ass

description: Guides for mods that integrate with Aetherhaven
text: For developers These pages explain how other mods can add content that works with Aetherhaven through asset packs and, when needed, small Java hooks. Start here Read for the folder map under Server/Aetherhaven/ , including: Villager definitions, dialogue trees, and weekly schedules Buildings, plot tokens, and schedule location symbols Quest patches, gift patches, and quest board entries A worked example you can copy into your own pack Players looking for addons Optional companion mods (Machinaria, Cozy Tales Fishing, and similar) are listed under in the wiki directory, not on this page. name: FAQ
description: Common questions about Aetherhaven, this wiki, and the community site
text: Frequently asked questions Answers here are meant as a quick reference while you play or browse the site. For deeper detail, open Mechanics or Villagers from the directory. How do I install the mod? Download Aetherhaven: Festivals of Orbis from and install it like any other Hytale mod for your server or world. How do I submit a community build? Sign in on with Sign in with Hytale , open My Submissions , and upload your plot prefab with screenshots and a description. Moderators review submissions before they appear in the public catalog. Will the mod have this feature? The answer is likely yes, but check the Roadmap page. Suggestions are always appreciated on the mod Discord. Where do I report bugs or suggest features? Bugs and feature requests can be submitted on the mod Discord channel. Including your game version and whether you are single-player or on a server saves a lot of back-and-forth. Will saves break when the mod updates? We try to keep data migrations safe, but back up your world before major updates, especially on long-lived servers. Can I design my own buildings instead of using the existing prefabs? Integrated building tools are a planned feature for the mod. There is a good amount of configuration that needs to go into adding buildings at the moment. You can destroy or replace a building after it is constructed, but note that breaking or moving certain furniture or benches may prevent villagers from using them to fill their needs. For example, moving a bed can stop a villager from finding it. There is a build submissions channel on Discord if you would like your build to be featured in the main mod with credit. What data does the website collect? The community site stores sign-in sessions, submission metadata, votes, and download counts as described on the page.

name: Getting Started
description: Found a town and learn the first steps
text: Getting Started This page is a short path from an empty spot in the world to a town that earns gold and welcomes villagers. Start your town 1. Craft a town planning desk at a workbench. 2. Use the desk to craft a town charter and a plot placement staff . 3. Place the charter where you want the heart of the town to be. Your town gets a random name at first. Open the charter later to rename it. 4. Lyren the Elder appears. Talk to him to begin. The charter marks your town borders. You can read more about moving or replacing it on the Town charter page under Mechanics. Your first quest: build the inn Lyren asks you to raise the inn . In practice that means: 1. Talk to Lyren and accept the quest. He gives you the inn plot token (plot tokens for building quests come from the quest giver, not the planning desk). 2. Equip the plot placement staff and stake the inn footprint where it fits. 3. Bring the listed wood and stone to the plot sign and finish construction. When the inn is done, an innkeeper moves in. The inn is your first real building and a home base for town records. How the inn helps The inn is more than walls and a roof. Visitors can stay for a while. The inn holds up to two guests at a time. The guest list refreshes each morning unless you are working on a visitor quest that locks someone in place. The inn includes a town records shelf where you can check villager needs, invite friends to your town, and review gift history later on. Read Inn pool and visitors under Mechanics if you want the full picture on guests. Money and taxes Your town earns gold coins from a morning tithe . Each villager who counts as a resident pays based on how comfortable they are. Comfortable means their hunger , energy , and fun meters are in good shape. Tax collection runs while at least one member of your town is online. Open the treasury after you build a town hall to see coins add up and read a breakdown of who paid what. See Treasury and taxes under Mechanics for feast bonuses, policies, and other ways to earn more. Town hall and treasury After the inn is finished, talk to Lyren again. He offers raise the town hall . Build it the same way you built the inn: take the plot token from the quest, use the placement staff, then bring materials to the sign. The town hall holds the treasury block where your gold is stored. It also has another town records shelf and planning space. You need the hall if you want to deposit, withdraw, and study tax lines in one place. Who counts as a citizen Villagers become part of your town in two different ways. Workplace (required for a job in town) Build and finish the plot for their job (farm, shop, mill, and so on). Use the management block on that building to assign the villager to the workplace. Until they have a workplace, they are a guest or visitor, not a full resident tied to that job. House (optional) A house plot is not required for them to work. If you build a house and register them on it, they can sleep there at night. Sleep refills energy , which also helps the gold they pay each morning. For fun , build a park (see below). When you are ready to grow, take quest offers from villagers and visitors at the inn. Each new workplace you finish can add another resident. Tips Build a park if villagers often run low on fun . Park benches are the main way to refill fun. Open Mechanics and read the Villager needs page for hunger, energy, and fun in detail. Talk to villagers often and bring gifts if you want better prices, recipes, and milestone rewards. See Reputation under Mechanics. After the town hall , read Mechanics for the guild hall and guards , quest board , tourist portal , and other mid-game systems. Server hosts can use creative mode tools such as /ah starterkit to skip crafting. That is for testing, not the normal player path.

name: Alchemy and flasks
description: Craft reusable flasks, discover mixtures and control brew quality
text: Alchemy and flasks Recruit Orin Glasswick from Town Level 5 and finish his Laboratory . The cauldron is your hands-on brewing station; the Alchemy workplace is the separate Townsfolk recipe system. Your first flask Use the large cauldron inside the completed Laboratory and choose Craft flask . A flask costs 5 Iron Ingots, 5 Light Leather and 5 Tree Sap, taken from your inventory first and then from town storage. There is no recipe to learn. A new flask is empty and holds one charge. Bring the flask and ingredients to the large cauldron inside the completed Laboratory. Choose an available ingredient from your inventory or town storage. Fill flask bottles the mixture at once as a Good potion. Hold the brew steady For a better potion, choose Start brewing first. A brew lasts 10 beats, and each press of a button is one beat. The heat rises by itself every beat. Stoke raises it faster and Stir cools it. A glowing band drifts along the heat gauge, and a beat counts when the heat marker ends inside it. The small arrows show where each choice would put the heat, and the pale outline shows where the band is heading. - Good, five or fewer beats in the band: the listed duration and restoration. - Great, six to eight beats: lasting effects run 25% longer; Health, Mana and Stamina restoration increases by 10%. - Perfect, nine or ten beats: lasting effects run 50% longer; restoration increases by 20%. Nothing is spent until you fill a flask, so you can brew again as often as you like, and you can stop and bottle a Good potion at any moment. Each extra ingredient in the mixture makes the band narrower and quicker. Orin's Mastery makes it wider. The quality stays with the potion until the flask is empty and is shown on the flask. Changing ingredients starts a new brew. Bottling discovers the selected ingredients' properties for your town. Health, Mana and Stamina plants restore those resources, with stronger plant tiers giving stronger effects. Some mushrooms provide temporary protection or increase maximum health or mana. Explore their properties at the cauldron. When two ingredients give the same kind of effect, only the stronger effect applies. Wild flowers are worth trying too. Blue Aloe and green mushrooms heal you slowly over time, with rarer green mushrooms healing more. A Fire Flower keeps fire and lava from harming you for a short while. Lavender and Chrysanthemum make a bug repellent, so scaraks, spiders and scorpions leave you alone until you attack one. The Florist sometimes stocks these flowers. Each drink consumes one saved charge. An empty flask can be filled again. To replace a mixture before it runs out, choose Empty flask at the cauldron; its remaining potion is lost. If you carry several flasks, use Next to choose one. Laboratory upgrades The cauldron begins with one ingredient slot. Open Building upgrades to buy a second slot with Alchemist Mastery 3 and 150 treasury gold , then a third with Mastery 6 and 350 treasury gold . These let you combine different effects in one mixture. Orin earns Mastery XP when you bottle mixtures. You can also train him through his Profile, where each Verdant Catalyst adds one level. Flask capacity Upgrade the selected flask at the cauldron. Each purchase adds one maximum charge and keeps the potion already inside. It does not refill the flask. - Two charges: Alchemist Mastery 2 and 5 Light Leather. - Three charges: Mastery 4 and 10 Medium Leather. - Four charges: Mastery 6 and 15 Heavy Leather. - Five charges: Mastery 8 and 20 Storm Leather. Filling a flask consumes one of each selected ingredient per charge . A five charge flask with three ingredients therefore needs five of each ingredient. The cauldron spends them only when the flask is filled. Apprentice brewing Orin also supervises Alchemy workplaces. name: Apprentice workplaces
description: Unlock, mark and staff each kind of Townsfolk workplace
text: Apprentice workplaces Workplaces are areas you mark for employed civilian Townsfolk. Named core villagers supervise their unlocks, but do not replace the workers. A workplace may be anywhere inside town; it need not be inside its supervisor's building. Set up your first workplace 1. Recruit the supervisor and finish their work building. Ask about Apprentice workplaces and unlock the desired type. Elder Lyren's A Place to Work quest helps you begin. 2. Craft a Building Staff at the Town Planning Desk. Any tier can manage workplaces. 3. Choose Create workplace from the staff's mode menu and mark two opposite ground corners. Choose a name and type, then save. 4. Place the type's required station inside the marked area. Keep its base within the floor and height, and leave a walking route to it. 5. Employ a civilian Townsfolk with the required skill. Enable the exact work type on the journal's Work page and keep wages paid. 6. Open the station or use Manage workplace . Queue a task, choose a growing plan or prepare a food-support site as its guide describes. The Blacksmith starts with two shared slots for Smelting, Blacksmithing and Armor Crafting. Other supervisors start with one. Capacity upgrades add slots; the upgrade screen shows Town Level and treasury costs. A slot belongs to the supervisor's allowance, not to an individual worker. Pick a workplace - Smelting workplace — Blacksmith; Furnace. Apprentices load furnaces, supply your selected fuel and collect the finished materials. - Blacksmithing workplace — Blacksmith; Blacksmith's Anvil. Apprentices forge weapons, tools and unlocked profession equipment. - Armor Crafting workplace — Blacksmith; Armorer's Workbench. Apprentices make armor and guard kits for the town. - Farming workplace — Farmer; Farmer's Workbench. A tended Farming workplace adds 10 food points , enough to support five residents . It produces no inventory items . - Ranching workplace — Rancher; Feeding Trough. A tended Ranching workplace adds 10 food points , supporting five residents . It produces no inventory items . - Mycologist workplace — Druid; Mushroom Log. Apprentices seed logs, tend growing mushrooms and harvest ingredients for cooking and Alchemy. - Berry Patch workplace — Druid; Farmer's Workbench. Apprentices tend berry bushes and collect ripe berries as inventory items. - Mining workplace — Miner; Workbench. Apprentices excavate real tunnels, stairs and rooms, then carry mined drops back to their base. - Builder's Yard workplace — Builder; Builder's Workbench. Apprentices travel to your town's construction projects and help build reachable pieces. - Block Workshop workplace — Builder; Builder's Workbench. Apprentices make planks, bricks, stairs, slabs, roofs and other building blocks to order. - Alchemy workplace — Alchemist; Alchemist's Workbench. Apprentices brew queued potion recipes from plants, petals, mushrooms and other supplies. - Crafting workplace — Crafter; Workbench. Apprentices make supplies, repair items, equipment and unlocked seed or sapling recipes. - Leatherworking workplace — Leatherworker; Tanning Rack. Apprentices turn hides into leather and make unlocked leather goods and profession equipment. - Cooking workplace — Chef; Chef's Stove. Apprentices cook food items from queued recipes. - Jewelry Crafting workplace — Merchant; Jewelry Crafting Bench. Apprentices make unlocked jewelry recipes, including equipment learned through friendship. - Salvaging workplace — Crafter; Salvager's Workbench. Apprentices dismantle old weapons, armor and tools into recovered materials. Logistics and couriers and Commerce and shop clerks have priority controls but do not need marked workplace areas. Herb Cultivation is retired; use the Druid's Spirit Garden for core alchemical plants. Existing hand-planted crops remain ordinary plants. name: Backpacks
description: Craft, open and upgrade portable storage
text: Backpacks A backpack is a portable store whose contents belong to that particular bag. It is separate from a Townsfolk's profession equipment. Get your first bag 1. Recruit Hazel Brindle , the Leatherworker, and complete her Tannery . 2. Talk to Hazel and open her backpack workshop. Craft a Simple Backpack for 10 Light Leather . Materials can come from your inventory and available town storage. 3. Hold the backpack and use it to open its contents. Click carried items to store them and stored items to take them out. Use Choose bag if you carry more than one. Rename bags to keep different supplies organized. Store matching deposits carried items of kinds already in the selected bag. Backpacks cannot be put inside other backpacks. Capacity and upgrades Return to Hazel with the bag you want to upgrade. Select the bag and an upgrade to see its exact materials before purchasing. Its contents stay with it. - Simple: 15 slots, one normal stack per slot. - Iron: 20 slots, one stack per slot. - Cobalt: 30 slots, one stack per slot. - Thorium: 20 slots, two stacks per slot. - Adamantite: 40 slots, three stacks per slot. Simple upgrades to Iron. From Iron, choose Cobalt for more slots or Thorium for deeper stacks. Either path can reach Adamantite. Compression I, II and III each add another normal stack per slot. Install an Item magnet , then turn it on in the backpack to collect nearby dropped items. A Travelling jukebox adds music selection and a stop button. These are optional upgrades, not extra storage tiers. If a purchase fails, check materials, free inventory space and which bag is selected. Stay near Hazel while crafting or upgrading.

name: Barn and owned animals
description: Buy animals, prepare pens, supply food and collect resources
text: Barn and owned animals Complete Thalen Meadowrun's Barn and finish his recruitment quest. The core barn keeps purchased animals and produces inventory items. Townsfolk Ranching workplaces provide population food support with their own automatic animals instead. Choose and assign animals Choose Animal shop when speaking to Thalen to open his separate shop. Common animals cost 100 gold at Rancher Mastery 1, uncommon animals cost 250 gold at Mastery 4, and rare animals cost 500 gold at Mastery 7. Ask Thalen about Building upgrades to unlock more pens and improve the barn. Food is shown as a small corner badge on each animal portrait. Resource storage starts at 10 per resource and gains 10 with each storage upgrade. Existing excess stock stays available to collect. Your barn starts with one active pen. Building upgrades unlock up to five pens. Choose Choose on a pen to open a grid of animal cards showing their picture, name, hearts and preferred food. Select a card to assign that animal. Choosing an animal already in another pen swaps the two animals. Rest empties a pen without losing its animal. Animals keep their names and hearts while resting. Rename them from My animals . Animals stay at their marked pen and cannot be killed or captured. You do not need to bring wild animals, find a breeding pair or raise offspring. Building authors mark five animal pens in the building editor by clicking the floor where each animal should stand. Face the direction it should look. Use Adjust or remove on a marker to remove it. Older community barns without pen markers automatically look for clear floor spaces inside the barn. Each automatic pen needs a 3 by 3 floor with four clear blocks above it. The pen screen tells you when space is missing. Your animals and upgrades stay yours; updated building designs use their author's pen positions. Daily food and hearts Each active animal eats one serving of its own food each day, beginning at dawn. Choose Supply all in the Food bin to transfer as much of that food as fits, up to 64 servings per type. Couriers can also supply it from farm output and town storage. Automatic deliveries keep eight of each active food by default. Choose a different target or turn deliveries off using the courier button. You need a Warehouse Manager and a townsfolk worker with Logistics enabled. Common animals eat early crops: Chicken: Corn, Farming Bench tier 2 Pig: Turnip, tier 3 Rabbit: Carrot, tier 2 Sheep: Lettuce, tier 1 Goat: Cauliflower, tier 3 Uncommon animals eat later crops: Cow and Deer: Pumpkin, tier 4 Boar and Camel: Aubergine, tier 4 Tetrabird: Tomato, tier 5 Skrill: Chilli, tier 5 Rare animals need the latest vegetables or meat: Bear: Raw wildmeat Mosshorn: Onion, tier 7 Moose and Armadillo: Potato, tier 7 These tiers refer to the ordinary seed recipe at the Farming Bench. Wheat is not animal food. Feeding gives 20 affection. Use the interaction prompt on an animal to pet it for another 10 affection, once each day. Each 100 affection earns a heart, up to five hearts. Each heart adds 20% to resource yields over time. Naming, resting or moving an animal does not reset its daily care. Animal resources Active, fed animals produce all their resources every six hours of loaded game time. Production speed upgrades shorten this interval. Hearts increase yields. Chickens and Skrills give eggs. Cows give beef, medium hide and milk. Sheep give wildmeat, light hide and wool. Tetrabirds give wildmeat and dark feathers. Armadillos give wildmeat and sturdy chitin. Other animals give their normal meat and hide. All animals slowly produce poop. Open Resources to see each product's stored amount and capacity, including products that are still empty, and collect supplies. Bring an empty bucket for each milk bucket you collect. Full storage pauses the next resource bundle until there is enough room for every item. Animals that are resting, waiting for food or outside loaded chunks do not produce. name: Block palettes for modders
description: Add Block Palettes from another mod
text: Block palettes for modders Other mods can unlock and remapping looks for their own blocks. Aetherhaven merges every JSON under Server/Aetherhaven/BlockPalettes/ from all asset packs. Easy path: remap groups Ship a JSON file in your pack, for example Server/Aetherhaven/BlockPalettes/mymod walls.json : Each variant becomes an unlockable Block Palette item. When a player picks Birch, any block whose id starts with MyMod Oak Wall is rewritten to the same trailing text under MyMod Birch Wall . Examples: - MyMod Oak Wall → MyMod Birch Wall - MyMod Oak Wall Stairs → MyMod Birch Wall Stairs - MyMod Oak Wall Half → MyMod Birch Wall Half Use the longest shared prefix you can so related pieces stay grouped. Missing target blocks are left alone. Categories can be existing ones ( walls , trunks , planks , cobble , bricks , cloth , roofs , cloth roofs , windows ) or a new id of your own. Adding looks that follow vanilla naming If your blocks already match Aetherhaven naming (for example more Wood Planks species), you can list them under categories with a familyKey and skip remap groups: A bricks palette can also point at a metal set. Use "familyKey": "metal:<Set " , for example metal:Goblin Iron , and each brick shape is swapped for the same shape of Metal <Set (block, smooth, ornate, decorative, half, smooth half and stairs). Shapes the metal set does not have, such as walls, beams and pillars, are left alone. Metal roofs are listed under roofs with "familyKey": "metal roof:<Set " . Java API After Aetherhaven has loaded, register from your plugin setup: You can also call catalog.register(new BlockPaletteDefinition(...)) for a single palette. Giving and unlocking Unlocked lists are per town. Players use the Block Palette item, or creative hosts can run /ah palette give <paletteId .

name: Building staff
description: Finish construction block by block
text: Building staff After a plot sign exists, the building staff lets you grow the structure in stages. Aim at highlighted blocks and confirm each batch. After pressing BUILD on a a plot sign, the building will start to build itself slowly. Using a Building Staff lets you speed up this process. While holding the staff green cubes will appear where blocks need to be placed. Holding secondary action (Right mouse button) with the staff while looking at these cubes will cause the cubes to expand and place the blocks for the building. If you can't find any green cubes you can use the primary action (Left mouse button) to shoot a projectile that homes in on the closest green cube. There are multiple tiers of building staff with increasing radius of building with the staff. Each staff grants extra max mana while you hold it. Placing blocks with secondary costs 1 mana per block from your mana bar. If you stop using secondary for a couple of seconds, mana refills faster while you still hold the staff. Tips Use scaffolding to reach higher places with the staff. Very large buildings are split into sections when building for performance. Plan a mineshaft Use Create workplace to mark a Mining base around a regular Workbench . Use that bench to open the map and plan tunnels, rooms and stairs into undug ground. The staff's Manage mineshafts mode reopens existing mine planners. Review each route before adding it. See Apprentice workplaces for worker, fitting and output storage details.

name: Town charter
description: Found and grow your town
text: Town charter The charter is your town anchor. Craft it at the town planning desk , then place it once to create the town, choose a name, and spawn Lyren the Elder to begin. What the charter does Marks your town borders in the world. Starts the founding quest line (inn, town hall, and beyond). Can be opened later to rename the town. If a town has no owner, anyone can open the charter and claim it. After placement, talk to Lyren to accept raise the inn and receive your first inn plot token . You stake that token with the plot placement staff the same way as every other building. Giving up a town Use /aetherhaven town relinquish to leave. If you are a member, you simply leave. If you are the owner, the town passes to another member. If you are the only person, the town keeps going with no owner, and someone else can claim it at the charter. Moving or removing the town You can move the charter from its menu if you need to adjust the town heart. If you dissolve the town, villagers and town buildings are removed with it. Read Getting Started for the full early-game path from charter to treasury. Tips If you dissolve the town, all villagers and buildings will be removed. You can move the charter using the button in its menu.

name: Clinic and recovery
description: Supply medicine and help injured residents recover
text: Clinic and recovery Recruit Elara Willowmere from Town Level 4, build her Clinic and complete recruitment. Set up care Talk to Elara and choose Let us check the clinic . The medicine cabinet accepts Lesser Health Potions from your inventory. Each bottle supplies 80 medicine , and the cabinet holds 800 . Medicine is spent only when someone receives healing. Bring injured guards into the clinic with Follow , then ask them to Wait Here . Elara treats one nearby resident at a time, seeing the most seriously injured first. Both people must remain inside the clinic and close together. Twelve quiet seconds restore up to forty health. Fighting and new injuries interrupt treatment. Elara also needs to take breaks for food and rest. The clinic cannot revive the dead. Visit the Gaia Altar for revival. Guards also recover slowly when resting safely. After thirty quiet seconds, they recover a little health every ten seconds. Clinic medicine provides faster recovery. The care screen shows Elara's availability and treatment progress while it is open. If treatment is waiting Read the care screen for medicine, availability and progress. Keep the patient and Doctor inside the Clinic, near each other, out of combat and able to reach the treatment area. Donate more Lesser Health Potions when medicine runs low. Injured civilian residents can seek care; use Follow and Wait Here to bring a guard in. The Clinic is a core specialist service, not a workplace type you assign in the priority grid. Guild hall and guards explains guard orders; Population and villager availability explains resurrection.

name: Commands
description: Chat commands for towns and server tools
text: Commands /aetherhaven and /ah are the same. Most players only need the For players section below. Access tells you which game mode gets the command by default. Permission is what server owners grant manually if access is not enough. Angle brackets are required; square brackets are optional. For players Town members - /ah town invite <player [townName] — Invite someone online to your town. - <player — Player username (must be online). - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.invite - Access: Adventure - /ah town accept [townName] — Join a town that invited you. - [townName] — Full town name when you have more than one pending invite. Omit if you only have one. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.accept - Access: Adventure - /ah town decline [townName] — Turn down a town invite. - [townName] — Full town name when you have more than one pending invite. Omit if you only have one. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.decline - Access: Adventure - /ah town kick <player [townName] — Remove a member from your town. - <player — Member username (must be online). - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your own town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.kick - Access: Adventure - /ah town role <player <role [townName] — Set a member role: BUILD, QUEST, or BOTH. - <player — Member username (must be online). - <role — BUILD , QUEST , or BOTH . - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your own town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.role - Access: Adventure - /ah town leave — Leave a town you belong to (not as the founder). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.leave - Access: Adventure - /ah town relinquish [townName] — Give up your town. Members leave. Owners pass it on to another member, or the town keeps going on its own if nobody else is left. - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit if you only belong to one town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.relinquish - Access: Adventure - /ah town style [townName] — Open the town look picker for building quests. - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your own town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.style - Access: Adventure - /ah town difficulty [townName] — Open the building cost difficulty menu for your town. - [townName] — Full town name with spaces. Omit for your own town. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.town.difficulty - Access: Adventure Floating gifts - /ah floatinggift next — See when your next floating gift balloon can appear. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.floatinggift.next - Access: Adventure Path tool - /ah path revert <id — Undo a cemented path using the id from chat when you placed it. You also need path tool access in play. - <id — Path revert id (UUID) printed in chat when the path was placed. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.path.revert - Access: Adventure For world hosts These are for creative mode or people running the server. Not needed for normal town play. - /ah difficulty — Open the building cost difficulty menu for your town (same as /ah town difficulty ). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.difficulty - Access: Creative - /ah reload — Reload mod config and data files from disk. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.reload - Access: Creative - /ah starterkit — Give yourself the starter tools (placement staff, charter, planning desk, building staff). - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.starterkit - Access: Creative - /ah exportskin [path] — Save your avatar skin as a model file. - [path] — Optional output path. Default is plugin data avatar exports with a timestamped filename. - Permission: hexvane.aetherhaven.command.aetherhaven.exportskin - Access: Creative - /ah exportsk

name: Miner's Hut and mining nodes
description: Renewable core mining and upgrading older designs
text: Miner's Hut and mining nodes Complete Gorruk Stonevein's Miner's Hut and recruitment quest. Core mining produces selected resources at renewable node locations. Mining workplace describes the separate Townsfolk mineshafts that excavate real terrain. Start production Open the mine's Production Storage, choose an unlocked output and check the stated Mastery and Pickaxe requirements. In a physical mine, keep authored node cells and standing space accessible. Gorruk must work the nodes during his shift and bring the goods back. Collect output there or from Building Outputs at the warehouse. Gorruk's own production requires both his Mastery and an equipped Pickaxe. Talk to him to train Mastery with Verdant Catalysts and equip a better tool from your inventory. He starts with a Crude Pickaxe. Iron needs Mastery 3 and Copper; Thorium and Cobalt need Mastery 5 and 6 respectively and Iron; Adamantite needs Mastery 8 and Thorium or Cobalt. Higher tools satisfy lower requirements. See Mastery and training for the full table. These requirements are separate from the Mining skill used by Apprentices below. Updating an older mine Existing mines keep their original production until you choose to update them. In Creative mode, aim the Building Editor Staff at your completed mine and press Use to review its new node layout. You must belong to the town and have permission to manage construction. The review starts with node locations from the currently installed building design. You can also choose Choose cells in this mine to make a local layout, even if the original design has no nodes. Use Mark on plain rock, ore or soil to select a cell. Use Adjust or remove on a selected cell to remove it. Ore previews show your selection, and the staff display shows your current controls. Use Open or confirm to review the plan, or crouch + Back to cancel. Review each location on the plan, or choose Show in world for temporary markers. The arrows let you inspect every node, including nodes above one another. Local changes apply only to this placed mine and do not change the downloaded building design. Putting the staff away hides the previews. Leaving the mine area, disconnecting or remaining idle for 30 minutes discards the selection. Apply node layout checks the blocks again and keeps your building, stored resources, selected outputs and purchased upgrades. It does not paste a fresh building. Changed blocks, furniture, storage or a lack of standing space prevent the update. The Miner must work at the nodes to produce resources after conversion. Updating a marketplace download alone never converts a placed mine. If mining stops Check the selected output, Gorruk's Mastery and equipped tool, storage room, the node blocks, standing space and his route. A broken tool needs repair. Apprentice Mining priority does not control Gorruk.

name: Farm and Scarecrow Fields
description: Plan Irienne's crops, collect harvests and care for soil
text: Farm and Scarecrow Fields Complete Irienne Mossmark's Farm and recruitment quest before planning her fields. This core farm grows inventory items. A marked Farming workplace instead has Townsfolk plant wheat for population food support. Irienne works the town's crops from a crop plan . You paint which crop goes where. She tills the ground, sows from the farm's seed store, waters, harvests and sows again, all by herself during her work hours while someone from town is nearby. 1. Use the farm's storage cupboard to open the field planner directly, or place a Farmer's Scarecrow on open ground anywhere in town and use it. Irienne gives you one Scarecrow when her farm is built, and more are crafted at the Town Planning Desk . 2. Pick a crop in the palette and select cells on the map. Double click a cell to paint its whole bed. Right click a cell to clear it. Fill field paints everything that is free. 3. That is all. Until you paint a plan a farm keeps its old automatic production. The first painted cell hands the farm to Irienne. The farm building has a field of its own. Every Scarecrow claims the ground around it as one more field with its own plan. Cells that cannot be farmed are dark on the map, and hovering over one says why. Seeds. A farm starts with a handful of wheat and lettuce seeds. Each cell uses one seed when it is sown, and a harvest gives its seed back about half the time. When the seed store runs out Irienne makes seeds from the Life Essence in the farm's stores, at the price of the game's own Farming Bench. Add seeds moves the seeds you carry into the store. Soil. Every cell is Worn, Good or Rich, shown by its colour on the map. - Good soil is ordinary soil. - Rich soil doubles every harvest and has a small chance of a Golden Harvest , which every villager loves as a gift and which sells for a high price. - Worn soil will not hold water, so crops grow slowly there. Growing the same crop in a cell six times running wears it one step. Sowing a different crop than last time lifts it one step, so Rotate crops once a day keeps most of a field Rich. Compost mends Worn soil. Compost. The farm keeps 25 of each crop. Crops beyond that are not wasted: three spare crops make one compost, and Irienne spreads it on Worn soil. The Almanac. Each week the Almanac favours a few of the crops Irienne can grow. A favoured crop is planted already sprouted and gives one extra crop at every harvest. The Almanac button shows this week and the next. Farm upgrades are paid with Life Essence and crops, from your pack first, then from the farm's stores and the warehouse. - More Scarecrows lets Irienne tend up to three Scarecrow fields. She starts with one. - Wider reach makes every Scarecrow field larger. - Better watering wets the cells around the one she waters. - Seed saving makes every harvest give its seed back. - Richer compost needs fewer crops, and at its second level makes Good soil Rich. - Almanac insight favours a third crop each week, then shows a whole season ahead. Each crop needs the Farmer's Mastery and unlocks shown in the palette. Collect harvests from the field planner's stores or the warehouse's Building Outputs; the farm no longer opens a separate Building Output screen. Crops inside Apprentice workplaces are not Irienne's: Apprentice farms feed the town and never produce items. A farm that already did field work before this change keeps working with its beds as its plan. When a field is waiting Hover a dark or blocked cell for its reason. Check the crop plan, seeds or Life Essence, Irienne's Mastery, walking access, work hours and output space. A Scarecrow must belong to your town and fit within the farm's field allowance. Crops in Apprentice workplaces are reserved for their workers. See Farming workplace , Population and villager availability , and Warehouse and deliveries for the related systems.

name: Festivals
description: Holidays your town celebrates on the festival square
text: Festivals Build a festival square and your town gets a place to celebrate. Most days it is a quiet plaza with benches. On a festival day the whole square changes into that festival's build, and it changes back when the day is done. Getting a festival square Corin at the inn asks for one once the park is done. Take his token, place the festival square like any other plot, and let it finish building. It counts as a fun spot all year, so townsfolk and visitors come by even when nothing special is happening. Matching your square's style Festival builds automatically match the style of the Festival Square you placed . For example, a Stormwind square uses the installed Stormwind look for that holiday. If there is no matching look, it uses the core festival build. Changing your town's preferred style does not change the style of an existing square. If several looks match, you can choose one at the plot crafting bench. Use square style automatically clears that preference. Looks from another style cannot be applied to this square. At the end of the festival, your square returns to its usual design. On the day The square swaps to the festival build in the morning and swaps back at the end of the festival. A banner announces the festival by name when it opens, so you know to head over. Villagers who have a spot at the festival drop what they are doing and go stand there until it is over. Spot villagers and visitors at the square will sometimes break into a little dance. Everyone in town has something to say about the festival while it runs, so it is worth doing the rounds. Visitors from other worlds head to the square while the festival runs. The calendar shows a marker on every festival day. Hover it to see which festival it is. Your birthday shows a gift box. Building on the square The square is looked after by the town, so nobody can dig it up or build on it. You can still use everything on it and harvest anything growing there. Keep your own decorations outside the plot. The New Life Festival Early spring, from morning to evening. The Springheart Lettuce sits in the middle of the square. Throw life essence at the Springheart Lettuce and it pulls the essence in as it grows. Concentrated life essence counts for a lot more. When it is full, interact with it to pop it. It throws vegetable seeds and spring festival tickets, then the Springheart Lettuce itself is gone. You can keep feeding it after it is full. Extra essence makes the pop throw more seeds and tickets. Feed it a huge amount and it pops on its own. It only pops once, so gather your life essence before the festival and share the moment with everyone. The Priestess , Farmer , and Elder each have a place to stand, and a kweebec seed seller brings a cart for the day. Bring gold coins if you want to shop. Every villager has their own thing to say about it, so make the rounds before the day is over. The Pig Racing Festival Late spring, from morning to evening. Four pigs race down the track while the town cheers them on. The four pigs wait at the starting line for the whole festival. When a race ends they pause at the finish, then head back to the start for the next one. Talk to the race merchant to bet gold coins on a pig. You can pick 10, 25, 50, or 100 gold coins, then choose which pig you like. Anyone can place a bet before the race starts. When you are ready, ask the merchant to start it. Only one race runs at a time. When it ends, a banner at the top of the screen names the winning pig. If your pig wins, talk to the merchant again to collect spring festival tickets. Bigger bets pay out more tickets. If you lose, the merchant will say so, then you can bet on another race. The merchant also keeps a small shop that takes spring festival tickets. Expect ranch goods for now. The Elder , Innkeeper , Blacksmith , and Rancher each have a place to stand by the track. Visitors watch from stands outside the lanes. Every villager has their own thing to say about it, so make the rounds be

name: Floating gifts
description: Sky presents for active towns
text: Floating gifts Sometimes a wrapped gift drifts above town. Shoot it down before it floats away. Gifts come in three colors. Each color holds different treasures inside a matching gift box. White gifts often hold building blueprints, gold coins, and useful supplies. Green gifts hold jewelry, gold coins, and useful supplies. Red gifts hold two furniture pieces, a random decoration prop, gold coins, and useful supplies.

name: Geodes
description: Crack rocks for gems
text: Geodes Geodes are chunky rocks found rarely when mining ores and crystals. They can hold ores, crystal shards, and sometimes gems inside. Cracking geodes Take geodes to Garren Vale at the blacksmith shop . He cracks them open for a gold fee. Rewards vary by geode type. If your friendship with Garren is high enough, he teaches you to craft the Geode Anvil . That bench lets you open geodes yourself without paying the blacksmith each time. Related pages Blacksmith villager page for Garren's quests and friendship rewards. Jewelry under Mechanics if you want to use gems after cracking.

name: Guild hall and guards
description: Resident invitations, guard equipment, patrol routes, and command mode
text: Guild hall and guards The guild hall is where adventurers gather. Lyra Fairhollow asks you to raise it after the town hall is standing. See her villager page for the build quest. Once the hall is finished you can assign guards , draw patrol routes , and use the command post to direct them. Residents and guard duty Talk to adventurers at the guild hall to invite them to live in town . Each adventurer asks for the same move in items they would request as a tourist. Bring the items shown in their invitation to give them when they join. Invitations also need enough food capacity. The new resident can perform profession work or become a guard. Open any resident Townsfolk's profile , then choose Guard duty . Choose Knight, Archer, Rogue or Mage. Town Rank limits how many guards you can support. Changing an existing guard's class does not need another place. Choose Return to civilian life to free their guard place. The resident keeps their home, skills and saved work priorities. Guards do no profession work while on duty. They must recover from injuries and finish any carried delivery before changing duty. Guards need a route or orders to know where to go. Unassigned guards still defend nearby threats when they can. Attributes and equipment Attributes determine guard health, attack power, protection and movement. Knights favor Strength, Archers and Rogues favor Dexterity, and Mages favor Intelligence. Vitality improves health. Train learned Attributes with Gaia Shards through the profile. New guards receive starter equipment. Better guard kits equip a complete class set at once. An Iron Knight Kit includes iron armor, a sword and a shield. Create kit tasks at an Armor Crafting workplace . Choose a class and tier to see the bonuses, ingredients and requirements. Copper needs Blacksmithing 2 and Town Rank E. Iron needs Blacksmithing 4 and Rank D. Thorium needs Blacksmithing 6, Rank C and an Armorer's Workbench at tier 2. Couriers deliver supplies, then an Apprentice must work at the bench to complete the kit. Click the Guard kit card in a resident's profile to select a kit from your inventory or town storage. A swap returns their old kit to the same source slot. Return kit puts it in your inventory if there is room. A saved kit only provides bonuses while its matching guard class is on duty. Profession equipment has a separate slot. Following and escort orders Ask a guard from your town to Follow Me , then talk to them again to choose orders. Wait here keeps the guard at that location until you return and choose Follow me again . Waiting guards still count toward your follower limit and do not chase enemies or teleport after you. Defensive responds when a creature attacks you. The guard will not start a fight just because a hostile is nearby or because you hit a harmless animal. Offensive engages nearby hostile creatures automatically. This is the default stance. Friendly town residents and players remain protected. Stop Following releases the escort and lets the guard return to normal duties. Your choice of combat stance remains when you pause and resume following. Explicit command-post orders replace following orders. Patrol wand Craft the patrol wand at the town planning desk . Blue sparkles mark saved routes only while you hold the wand. The game shows your own key for each action below at the bottom right of the screen. Build mode (default) Add or remove point on the ground: add a patrol point. Add or remove point on a point: remove it. Select route on a point of a saved route: select that route for editing. Mode action : name and save the route (needs at least two points). Crouch + Next mode : toggle closed loop (guards loop from last point back to first) vs back and forth . Reset : start a fresh route. Next mode : switch to Assign mode. Assign mode Select route on a route point: select a saved route. Mode action : open the guard list and assign someone to the route. Reset : clear the guard from the selected route. Next mode : sw

name: Hunter's Lodge and arena
description: Set up the arena, start creature runs and collect spoils
text: Hunter's Lodge and arena Recruit Kael Thorne from Town Level 4, build his Hunter's Lodge and finish recruitment. Talk to Kael to open his hunt controls. Set up the arena The Hunt Beacon marks the centre of the arena. Keep a clear 9 by 9 floor around it with room overhead. The beacon must stay inside the completed lodge plot. Unlock creatures with treasury gold and samples of their drops. Choose Start to begin a run. Kael fights one creature at a time, collects its spoils and faces progressively stronger opponents. Runs never begin automatically and do not progress while the world is unattended. Skeletons provide bones and linen scraps. Goblin Scrappers provide Scraps, which Tobin uses for props. Frost undead also provide Ice Essence. Burnt and incandescent undead provide Cindercloth and Fire Essence. Outlanders provide Shadoweave. Void Crawlers and the larger Void Spawn provide Void Essence and can drop Voidhearts. Spoils follow the creature's normal drop chances and amounts, excluding weapons, armor and tools. Collected spoils stay safe when a run ends. Open the lodge's Production Storage to browse and collect spoils, or collect them through the town warehouse. Make space when the spoils racks fill. Couriers can use lodge supplies for workplace orders. When creating or editing a Hunter's Lodge, the creator and editor require both the Hunt Beacon and Production Storage inside its bounds. Select the beacon to see Hunt portal opens here , Creature entrance and Hunter's starting position markers. Their positions follow the building's orientation, not the beacon block's facing. Leave the whole 9 by 9 arena clear. Training Spend treasury gold on vitality, power, field dressing, Second Wind and larger spoils racks between runs. Training improves Kael's survival and lets him complete longer runs. If a run will not start Check the completed lodge, beacon, clear 9 by 9 floor, overhead room, Kael's availability and output capacity. Unlock and select creatures before ordering a run. Use the creator/editor markers when changing a design so the portal and fighters have space. Each new run needs your order.

name: Inn pool and visitors
description: Rotating guests at the inn
text: Inn pool and visitors The inn can host visitors who are not full-time residents. Visitors appear in the inn commons, offer quests, and may later ask for workplaces of their own. Capacity and refresh The inn holds up to two visitors at a time. The guest list rerolls at dawn each day unless a visitor is locked by an active quest. If you have accepted a visitor's quest, that visitor stays until you finish the quest line they started. The inn also includes a town records shelf for needs, invites, and gift history. Read Getting Started for how the inn fits into founding a town. Full residents vs visitors A villager with a finished workplace plot assigned on the management block counts as a resident for taxes and schedules. Visitors at the inn are guests until you build their job plot and assign them. Guest Book At Town Level 3, buy the Guest Book through Corin's Building Upgrades for 100 treasury gold . Its dialogue option appears after unlocking it. The book shows only available villagers, ordered by required Town Level. Each invitation costs 50 treasury gold and requests the next free morning guest spot. Debugging If the inn's visitors do not appear or look wrong, try running /ah villager fixinn (see Commands under Mechanics).

name: Jewelry
description: Rings, necklaces, and stats
text: Jewelry Jewelry can occasionally be found in loot chests. Bring unidentified pieces to Vex the Merchant or an Appraisal Bench to reveal their effects. Gold is stronger than silver, and necklaces are stronger than rings. Apprentice jewelry crafting Recruit the Merchant, then unlock Jewelry Crafting through his building upgrades. Mark a workplace using the Building Staff and place a Jewelry Crafting Bench inside it. The bench is a work surface for Apprentices. It no longer opens a player crafting menu. Enable Jewelry Crafting for an employed townsfolk in the journal. Create tasks at the workplace and let couriers deliver the materials. Rings use five metal ingots and necklaces use ten, plus one gemstone. Higher quality plans require more life essence and a higher Jewelry Crafting skill: Common 1, Uncommon 3, Rare 5, Mythic 7 and Legendary 10. The task menu shows the exact requirements. Place an Appraisal Bench inside the same workplace to reveal completed jewelry automatically. Extra appraisal benches do not stack or improve quality. Without one, crafted jewelry still needs appraisal. Completed pieces go to Crafted Goods in town storage. Maintain targets count the chosen jewelry quality. Gemstone stats Each gemstone type sets which three player stats the piece can roll. The exact numbers depend on rarity, metal, and ring vs necklace. Zephyr : Stamina, Signature Energy, Oxygen Topaz : Stamina, Signature Energy, Ammo Emerald : Health, Mana, Oxygen Diamond : Health, Stamina, Mana Sapphire : Mana, Stamina, Oxygen Ruby : Health, Stamina, Ammo Voidstone : Mana, Signature Energy, Ammo Tips Extra jewelry makes great gifts for villagers. See Reputation under Mechanics for how gifting affects friendship.

name: Lumbermill and Singing Grove
description: Bind Rootstones, grow trees and collect timber
text: Lumbermill and Singing Grove Complete Seren Fairhollow's Lumbermill and her recruitment quest. Seren works the grove herself; Townsfolk work priorities do not assign her trees. Seren grows the town's wood on Rootstones . She gives you two when her lumbermill is finished. Craft more at the Town Planning Desk from stone, Life Essence and fibre. 1. Place a Rootstone on open ground anywhere inside your town. 2. Use the Rootstone and pick one of the saplings you carry. It takes one sapling. 3. Seren does the rest during her work hours. She plants the tree, sings it tall, fells it and carries everything back to the lumbermill. The stone then grows the same tree again for free, for as long as you leave it there. Any of 32 trees works once you own its sapling. A tree needs open space above and around its Rootstone. If there is not enough room, the Rootstone tells you what is in the way. Trees from different Rootstones cannot grow into each other, so give large trees plenty of space. Seren can tend two Rootstones at first. Lumbermill upgrades let her tend up to six, sing faster and store more. Open the lumbermill's stores, or any Rootstone, to see every stone at a glance. From there you can also: - Bless a Rootstone. Spend 5 Life Essence and its next tree gives double wood. - Uproot a tree. This frees the Rootstone so you can choose another tree or move the stone. A tree that is already standing stays where it is and becomes yours to chop. A stone that has not been planted yet returns its sapling. - Collect all. Take everything in the mill stores. You are free to trim or build around a grove tree. Seren simply harvests what is left of it. Breaking a Rootstone frees it in the same way as uprooting. A lumbermill that worked the old way keeps doing so until its first Rootstone is given a sapling. From then on Seren works the grove instead, and that cannot be undone. Training and troubleshooting Talk to Seren to train her Mastery with Verdant Catalysts and equip a Hatchet from your inventory. She starts with a Crude Hatchet. Each timber's requirement follows its sapling's Farming Bench tier. Tier 4 needs Iron, tiers 5 and 6 need Thorium or Cobalt, and tiers 7 and above need Adamantite. Higher tools satisfy lower requirements. Each Rootstone tells you when Seren needs more Mastery or a better tool for its tree. See Mastery and training for the full progression. Keep the stone and its future tree space clear, including overhead. A Rootstone reports obstacles, Mastery and tool requirements. Check Seren's shift, walking access and room in the lumbermill's stores. She must bring the harvest home before you can collect it. Building Outputs in the warehouse also exposes stored mill resources. Couriers can use that timber for queued recipes.

name: Mastery and training
description: Train specialists, equip tools and spend Townsfolk points
text: Mastery and training Resident specialists The Miner, Logger, Farmer, Rancher, Druid and Alchemist each have Mastery from 1 to 10 . Talk to the resident and choose View your profile . Completed production earns Mastery XP when goods reach storage. The Alchemist earns XP when you bottle a mixture. The ten segments show the current level, and a second bar shows XP toward the next level. Each level needs more XP than the last. One Verdant Catalyst raises Mastery by exactly one level and keeps any earned XP. Their production storage shows any requirement that blocks an output. Every resident's profile shows your reputation, its reward milestones and the gift preferences you have discovered by giving gifts. Villagers who do not use Mastery only show their friendship information. Reward contents remain a surprise until you unlock their milestone. Claim ready rewards through normal dialogue. Profiles opened from the Town Journal have a button to return there. The Miner starts with a Crude Pickaxe and the Logger with a Crude Hatchet . Bring a better tool in your inventory and equip it through the profile's Equipment tab. Replacing an equipped tool returns that tool to your inventory with its condition preserved. Higher tool tiers satisfy lower requirements. A broken tool must be repaired before work can continue. Mining requirements Resource Miner Mastery Pickaxe --- --- --- Copper and ordinary stone 1 Crude Iron 3 Copper Silver 4 Copper Thorium 5 Iron Cobalt 6 Iron Gold 7 Iron Adamantite 8 Thorium or Cobalt Mithril 10 Adamantite Timber and growing requirements Timber Mastery follows the sapling's Farming Bench tier, with a minimum of 1. Sapling tiers 0 to 2 need a Crude Hatchet, tier 3 needs Copper, tier 4 needs Iron, tiers 5 and 6 need Thorium or Cobalt, and tiers 7 and above need Adamantite. A Rootstone tells you when the Logger needs more training for its tree. Farm crops use their seed's Farming Bench tier for the Farmer's Mastery requirement. The Druid needs Mastery 1, 4 and 7 for alchemical plant tiers 1, 2 and 3 . The Rancher needs Mastery 4 for medium hides and red feathers, and 7 for heavy hides. Stored output and material already being carried remain available while you train. Townsfolk Townsfolk earn Mastery experience by completing profession work, including crafting, deliveries, building and food care. Their Mastery rises from 1 to 20 , with more experience needed at each level. Each level gained awards one skill point . Levels 5, 10, 15 and 20 also award two attribute points . Open the Townsfolk's profile and spend points beside the attribute or profession you want to improve. Each point adds one level. You can also spend one Gaia Shard for one attribute level or one Verdant Catalyst for one profession level. Training items do not raise Townsfolk Mastery. A profession at zero remains unavailable. Profession skills have a maximum of 10 , and attributes have a maximum of 20 . A worker's skill, workplace equipment and recipe requirements all still apply. Mastery progress and trained abilities remain with the same person through resurrection.

name: Path designer shovel
description: Lay out spline paths, styles, and removal
text: Path designer shovel The path designer shovel lets you draw curved paths through town, preview them, and place blocks on the ground. A status panel appears while you hold the tool. It names each action, and the game shows your own key for each one at the bottom right of the screen. If the keys are missing, turn on Display Input Bindings in HUD in the game settings. Craft it at the town planning desk . Modes Use Next mode to cycle through modes: 1. Move — add and reposition control nodes to shape the path. 2. Rotate — turn the selected node to bend the spline. 3. Place — cement the finished path onto the ground. 4. Remove — view placed paths (highlighted in orange) and delete ones you no longer want. 5. Restyle — select a placed path and swap its blocks to another style. 6. Replace filter — choose which ground blocks the path may replace. 7. Style designer — create and edit path styles in a chest grid. The HUD reminds you to switch to Place mode when you are ready to lay path blocks. Controls by mode Move, Rotate, and Place Add or remove on the ground: add a node. Add or remove while looking at a node: remove that node. Select while looking at a node: select it. Select on the ground (Move mode): move the selected node. Mode action (Rotate mode): nudge the selected node's direction. Mode action (Place mode): place the path on the ground. Width or save : open path width settings. Crouch + Next mode : open the style list. Mode menu : open the mode jump menu (also toggle whether townsfolk walk paths you place). Next mode : switch to the next mode. Remove Select while looking at a placed path: select it. Mode action : remove the selected path. Mode menu : open the mode jump menu. Next mode : switch to the next mode. Restyle Select while looking at a placed path: select it. Mode action : open the style list. Choosing a style swaps that path's blocks right away. Mode menu : open the mode jump menu. Next mode : switch to the next mode. Style designer Mode action : open the style manager (double-chest grid for weighted block columns). Width or save : save the path style (while the chest is open). Mode menu : open the mode jump menu. Next mode : switch to the next mode. Preview visuals While editing, white nodes and lines show the spline. A brown preview marks where blocks will go, with green edges at the sides. Remove and Restyle modes show committed paths in orange instead. Tips Shape the spline in Move and Rotate first, then switch to Place and use Mode action to cement it. Build custom looks in Style designer — each style is a weighted column of blocks rolled along the path width. Use Restyle when you want a different look on a path you already placed, without removing it first. Paths persist in the world and in your town save.

name: Tobin's Pattern Book
description: Learn prop patterns, commission copies and salvage props
text: Tobin's Pattern Book Recruit Tobin Reedwright and complete his Artisan Workshop . This is his own prop commission service, separate from the Crafting workplace and Salvaging workplace run by Townsfolk. Tobin can build any prop he has studied. Talk to him and choose Open your Pattern Book . 1. Show him a prop. Carry any prop and choose Show Tobin the props you carry . He sketches every new one into his book and hands them all back. The whole town shares his book. 2. Commission a copy. Pick a known pattern and choose Commission one . Props cost simple materials, never gold. 3. Collect it. Tobin builds the first prop on his bench during his work hours. Finished props wait on his shelf. Props Tobin has not seen yet show as a question mark. Cap'n Clive, treasure, gifts and festivals are good places to find new ones. Materials Every prop is made from four ordinary resources. Tobin takes them from your pack first, then from the town warehouse. - Sticks - Stone Rubble - Scraps - Linen Scraps Gather them as usual, or have Apprentices make them at a Crafting workplace. Their task list includes all four: 5 of any wood makes 10 Sticks, 5 of any stone makes 10 Stone Rubble, 5 of any metal bar makes 10 Scraps, and 10 fibre makes 5 Linen Scraps. The Logger's grove also brings home sticks with every tree, and goblins carry Scraps. A more valuable prop needs more materials and more time. The kinds it needs follow what it is made of. A plank shelf asks for Sticks and a weapon rack asks mostly for Scraps. Salvage Pick a prop you carry and choose Salvage one to have Tobin take it apart. You get half of its materials back, and he learns its pattern if he did not know it. Cancelling a commission returns everything. Collection goals - 5 patterns: a third commission on the bench. - 10 patterns: salvaging returns three quarters of the materials. - 20 patterns: a fourth commission on the bench. - 30 patterns: commissions take a quarter less time. If a commission is waiting Check the selected pattern, commission capacity, materials and Tobin's work hours. Finished props wait on his shelf until collected. Showing him a prop returns it; choosing Salvage one consumes it for materials.

name: Player shop and shop spots
description: Villager shops, your own shop, and buying in the world
text: Player shop and shop spots Shop spot blocks live inside finished building plots. They let NPCs and players sell items in the world instead of only through dialogue menus. NPC shops Villager shops — Vex's general store , the Florist, Pyrotechnic, Crystal Keeper, and others — restock at dawn from loot tables. Each shop spot shows a floating item display, and the way the shop spot faces turns the display. F (use) — open the buy panel with quantity controls (±1, ±10, max). Look-at HUD — shows item name, price, and stock while you aim at a stocked spot. Vex now runs a general store selling furniture, blocks, and consumables through shop spots in his market stall and related buildings. Your own shop Assign a civilian with Commerce through the shop's town records shelf. They must be employed, paid and attending the counter during daylight for visiting villagers and tourists to buy. Higher Commerce skill improves the chance of a purchase. Guard duty takes priority over shop work. Shop work pauses when no town member is in this world, alongside wages. After Vex's market stall is built, Vex offers Your Own Shop : 1. Take the player shop plot token from Vex. 2. Stake and build the player shop prefab. 3. Find Vex and close the quest in dialogue. The player shop includes shop spot blocks and a shop safe that holds gold from your sales. Listing items Use a shop spot while holding an item: list it for sale (player-controlled spots only). Use it again on your own listing: remove it from the spot. Buyers use stocked spots to purchase. You receive a notification when someone buys your listing, and gold collects in the shop safe . Who shops Villagers and tourists browse player shop spots and buy listed items when they visit town. Price and stock matter — empty spots are skipped. Permissions Town members need permission to sell on player shop spots. The town owner can adjust member permissions from the town records shelf. See Plot tokens under Mechanics for crafting plot tokens at the plot crafting bench.

name: Plot creator staff
description: Turn a build into a custom town building definition
text: Plot creator staff The plot creator staff registers custom buildings you built in the world: footprint, specialty blocks, prefab export, costs, and (optionally) a live plot in your town. Most players should use Decoration or Variant , not the full workplace types below. Open your town journal → Guide → Mechanics → Plot creator staff (this page) while learning the flow. In play: equip the staff, use Open or confirm to start or open the current step panel, use Mark on blocks in the world, Back / Continue for the previous / next step, Step menu to jump to a step you already reached, and crouch + Back to cancel. The game shows your own key for each of these at the bottom right of the screen. Recommended paths Goal Building type Notes ------ ---------------- ------- Cosmetic build, no jobs Decoration Optional town records shelf; no production or villager logic. Alternate look for an existing building Variant Pick which main building it counts as (house, barn, inn, etc.). Substeps follow that main type. New workplace / production plot (modding) Work For adding new workplace types; needs management block, production storage, and a work surface POI. Building types (picker) Decoration — Parks, props, and builds that should not act as homes, shops, or workplaces. Minimal required spots. Variant — A prefab that counts as another building id already in the mod (for example a custom house that counts as plot house ). You choose the main type from the dropdown; important spots match that main building. Home — Residential plot: town records shelf + sleep POI. Work — Developer / content author use. Defines a new workplace -style plot: town records shelf, production storage, and a work-surface POI. Use when you are adding a new production or job building type, not for normal cosmetic variants. Amenity — Fun or leisure (park, altar-style amenity): shelf + fun/sit POI. Shop — Villager shop with a counter: shelf + shop-tagged work POI, plus shop spots for the goods. Inn — Full inn layout: shelf, work surface, beds, eat spot, innkeeper and visitor spawns (and optional guild master spawn slot). Town hall — Civic hub: shelf, treasury block, planning desk POI. Guild hall — Adventurer guild: shelf, work surface, adventurer spawn points. Overlap and confusion - Variant vs Home / Work / … — Variant is for “looks different, behaves like X.” Pick Variant + main type, not Home , if you are reskinning an existing gameplay building. - Work vs Shop — Shop is for villager shops that sell from shop spots. Work is for farms, mills, forges, and other production workplaces. - Amenity vs Decoration — Decoration has almost no gameplay hooks. Amenity sets fun/amenity tags and POIs for villager schedules. - Inn , Town hall , and Guild hall are full templates; use Variant only if you are matching one of those templates on purpose. Flow (short) 1. Drag to mark the build box (the plot sign is placed at the center automatically). Stand inside the box and use Adjust or remove to expand one block toward where you look, or crouch + Adjust or remove to shrink. You can also drag the side panels. 2. Choose building type (and variant of if applicable). 3. Place important spots (blocks are given one at a time per substep). 4. Open building settings (F): name, id, tags, treasury gold cost, self build days, empty space prefab option, and other options. 5. Export prefab with F on the save shape step (uses settings from step 4). 6. Set build materials (virtual chest; items return to you when you continue). 7. Review and save. Choosing buildings for style quests In Building settings , enter the building's Style , then tick Preferred quest building for this style if quests should use this design. You can change this setting in the Building Editor too. For example, mark your farm design to make it the farm plot given by quests in towns using that style. The building must still count as a farm. If several matching designs are marked, the quest picks one at random. Marked designs take pri

name: Plot placement staff
description: Claim land and stamp building footprints
text: Plot placement staff The plot placement staff is how you stake where a new building will go. You receive one when you craft your first town charter at the town planning desk . How to use it 1. Hold a plot token for the building you want (from a quest giver or the plot crafting bench ). 2. Equip the plot placement staff. 3. Choose the construction type if prompted, then aim where the building should sit and confirm. The building preview uses that spot; the plot sign is placed at the center of the footprint on the ground below. 4. Bring materials listed on the sign and finish construction with the building staff or by waiting for auto-build. The staff only places footprints. It does not finish walls or assign villagers. Read Plot tokens for where tokens and blueprints come from, and Building staff for speeding up construction. Tips Story quests usually hand you the first token for a building. Replacements and extra copies often come from the plot crafting bench afterward. Some shop quests grant a plot blueprint instead of a ready token. Use the blueprint at the bench, craft the token, then stake with this staff.

name: Plot tokens
description: Items that unlock special builds
text: Plot tokens Plot tokens are items you hold in inventory to pick a building type on the plot placement staff , then stake the footprint in the world. Plot crafting bench Craft plot tokens at the plot crafting bench . The bench shows a 3D preview of the building before you commit materials. Craft the bench at the town planning desk , then place it like any workstation. Most story quests still hand you the first token directly from the quest giver. After that, replacements and extra copies usually come from the bench. Your town's building style Click Download to choose a town style and start its download. The menu closes so you can keep playing: a small HUD panel shows which building files are downloading, how many buildings remain, and how many resource-loading steps are complete. Builds requiring mods your server does not have are left out. Wait for Ready to use before choosing a newly downloaded building. If something fails, the panel names the problem and puts the details in chat so you can read them later and retry. When a quest gives you a plot token, it looks for an installed building in your town's chosen style. It first uses any matching buildings the author marked as preferred quest choices. Otherwise, it prefers a building that has only the requested purpose: a farm quest picks a farm-only building before a farm that also counts as a house or blacksmith. If there is no single-purpose option, it uses a matching mixed-use building. When several buildings qualify, one is chosen at random.
