If the style has no suitable installed building, you receive the default plot. Plot blueprints Some buildings are gated behind plot blueprints instead of dropping ready-made tokens from balloons. 1. Use the blueprint item to permanently unlock that plot at your plot crafting bench. 2. Open the bench and craft the plot token (materials plus gold, same as other tokens). 3. Equip the plot placement staff and stake the footprint. White floating gifts often carry blueprints. Green gifts favor jewelry; red gifts favor furniture and decoration props. Balloon gifts are rarer than before. Salvage Extra plot tokens — including variant tokens from gifts — can be salvaged for gold coins at a workbench when you do not need another copy. Tips Read Player shop and shop spots under Mechanics if a building includes shop spots. Florist, Pyrotechnic, and Crystal Keeper shop quests grant blueprints rather than direct tokens.

name: Population and villager availability
description: Food support, town levels, recruitment, and resurrection
text: Growing your town Your Town Journal shows current residents, food support, and progress to the next Town Level. Each resident needs 2 food points . Visitors do not count. Residents who have died keep their place until you revive them. The Inn provides 10 food points . The Elder and Innkeeper use four of those points, leaving room for three more residents. A completed farm, ranch, and restaurant each add another 10 food points . Building a second copy of the same core building does not multiply food support. When food support falls below your population, current residents stay. New invitations become unavailable until enough food support is restored. Each ready, tended Farming or Ranching workplace adds another 10 food points , supporting five residents. These sites produce no inventory items. Their bonus pauses after a full simulated day without tending and returns when care resumes. The neglect clock pauses when no town member is in the town's world. Cooking , Berry Patch and Mycologist workplaces produce items rather than this food-support bonus. Irienne's Wheat for the Town quest teaches Farming workplace setup, including the bench and four clear soil spaces. The townsfolk plant wheat themselves. Ask the Innkeeper about food supply and population for an in-game explanation, and see the individual Farming and Ranching workplace guides for setup and troubleshooting. Villager availability Earlier villagers remain available as your town grows. Building requirements still apply. Town Level 1 · 1 to 3 residents Farmer and Rancher become available. Town Level 2 · 4 to 6 residents Miner, Logger, Builder, Priestess, Guild Master, Chef and Warehouse Manager become available. Town Level 3 · 7 to 10 residents Blacksmith and Crafter become available. Town Level 4 · 11 to 15 residents Merchant, Leatherworker, Monster Hunter, Druid and Doctor become available. Town Level 5 · 16 to 20 residents Alchemist, Furniture Merchant, Florist and Bard become available. Town Level 6 · 21 or more residents Crystal Keeper, Pyrotechnic, and Clown become available. The Chef needs both a completed farm and a completed ranch before appearing at the Inn. Food villagers and the Guild Master receive priority when eligible visitor places are filled. Town Levels unlock civic growth. Town Ranks come from the Guild Hall and govern defense progression. They are separate systems. Townsfolk profiles Talk to a Townsfolk and open their profile to see five Attributes and twelve Profession Skills. Personalities and guard classes shape starting abilities. Profession skills range from 1 to 10. A zero means that person cannot do that profession. One Gaia Shard raises an Attribute by one, and one Verdant Catalyst raises a Profession Skill by one. Townsfolk also earn Mastery through completed work, up to level 20. Each level gained gives a skill point; levels 5, 10, 15 and 20 each give two attribute points. Spend these points in the profile. Training stays with that person through resurrection. See Mastery and training for details and the separate training of resident specialists. Resurrection The Gaia Altar hides residents who are present and alive. It can also bring back missing villagers. Townsfolk who have joined your town can be revived there, including guards. Reviving someone restores the same place in town, with their home and trained abilities preserved.

name: Production buildings
description: Choose between specialist production and Apprentice work
text: Production buildings Core production buildings belong to named specialists. Their work is separate from the priority-driven workplaces you mark for Townsfolk. Choose a system - Farm and Scarecrow Fields: Irienne grows planned crops for harvest items. - Barn and owned animals: Thalen cares for purchased, assigned animals that produce resources. - Lumbermill and Singing Grove: Seren grows and harvests trees at Rootstones. - Miner's Hut and mining nodes: Gorruk works renewable marked rock and ore. - Spirit Garden: Rowan grows alchemical plants and petals in Spirit Planters. - Hunter's Lodge and arena: Kael fights ordered creature runs for spoils. Finished production remains in each building's storage. Building Outputs at the warehouse lets you collect those stores without merging their capacity. Their own controls handle plans, unlocked choices and upgrades. The farm opens its field planner rather than a separate Building Output screen. A Townsfolk Farming or Ranching workplace adds population food support and produces no inventory items. Cooking makes meal items without adding food-support points. See Population and villager availability for town growth. Older community builds Older farms keep automatic production until you paint a crop plan. Old lumbermills keep it until the first Rootstone is given a sapling. Existing mines keep their original production until you apply a reviewed node layout. Older barns without animal markers automatically use suitable clear floor spaces, preserving owned animals and upgrades. If space is missing, the herd screen explains the requirement. Updated authored pen positions take precedence. Builders should use the Plot Creator or Building Editor to update specialty equipment and activity positions. Both guide required equipment for the selected building, including community variants. When production pauses Read the building's own status first. Check the resident's presence, shift, Mastery and tool, physical work area, path and storage capacity. Apprentice priorities do not assign a core specialist's work. Keep the relevant area loaded; these systems do not run a distant town for you.

name: Production wardrobe
description: Open each building's work controls and collect its stored output
text: Production wardrobe A core building's Production Storage opens the controls appropriate to that building. The town warehouse's Building Outputs also lets you collect resources while they remain in their original stores. What opens at each building - Farm: the Scarecrow Fields planner opens directly. Paint crops, supply seeds, review soil and collect harvests there. The separate Building Output screen is hidden. - Barn: use the herd controls to assign owned animals, supply food and view Resources. Production follows assigned, active animals, not a generic choice of outputs. - Lumbermill: manage Rootstones and collect grove output. Older mills retain their original production until their first Rootstone is bound. - Conservatory: open the Spirit Garden to manage planters and collect plants and petals. - Miner's Hut: choose unlocked resources and collect output. Physical mines require accessible nodes, the Miner's Mastery and an appropriate Pickaxe. - Hunter's Lodge: collect the spoils of ordered arena runs from lodge storage. Open Production buildings for dedicated setup pages. A Townsfolk Farming or Ranching workplace has no item-output cupboard: it contributes food support instead. Storage, unlocks and upgrades Collect all also recovers older stock whose resource is no longer selected. Milk needs empty buckets. Full storage can pause further production. Couriers can collect eligible resources for workplace tasks. Where a building has output choices, selecting a resource does not bypass its Mastery, tool or unlock requirements. Read the screen's missing requirement and train or equip the named specialist. Use the building's own upgrade controls for capacity, speed and its physical system. Farm, grove and garden upgrades affect their named fields, stones or planters. Warehouse upgrades do not expand every production store. Keep paths and work areas accessible and loaded. Core specialists follow their schedules; the Townsfolk priority grid controls Apprentice jobs.

name: Purification powder
description: Cleanse cursed jewelry rolls
text: Purification powder Purification powder lets you remove enemy spawn points inside generated structures. It is unlocked by befriending Serah , the Priestess . How to use it 1. Craft or obtain purification powder after the unlock. 2. Hold the powder in your hand. Small spinning mob markers appear where periodic spawns would occur in that structure. 3. Use the powder on a marker to remove that spawn point permanently. This is separate from jewelry cleansing rolls. Powder targets world structure spawners, not item stats. Read the Priestess villager page for her Gaia altar quests and friendship rewards.

name: Quest board
description: Daily fetch, hunt, and raid jobs at the guild hall
text: Quest board The quest board in the guild hall posts daily work for your town. Interact with the board to open a three-card panel showing today's jobs. New cards refresh each dawn when at least one member of your town is online. Job types Fetch A townsfolk needs supplies brought to town. Accept the job, gather the listed items, and turn them in through that villager's dialogue . Rank tiers gate harder requests and better rewards. Standard supply jobs include payment for the requested goods plus a delivery bonus. The board shows the full reward before you accept. That price stays fixed for the posted job, even if town shop prices change later. Special requests from other packs may set their own rewards. Hunt Kill a certain number of a mob type, then report back to the quest giver. Progress shows on the card and in your journal. Rescue Sometimes a townsfolk is tied up at a small camp outside town, held by goblins, trorks or outlanders. Accept the contract and follow the camp's marker on your compass. The captors and their prisoner are waiting when you get there. Defeat every captor, then use the interaction on the townsfolk to cut their ropes. Talk to them afterwards to finish the contract. You do not need to report back to the quest giver. The rescued townsfolk comes to live in your town. They skip the usual move in gift and still need a house. They are one level better than usual at two skills, and harder contracts bring someone better at up to five. Press Who is it? on the card to see their profile before you accept. Rescues are only posted while your town has room for another resident and no other house quest is under way. The camp disappears afterwards and the land is put back as it was. Mining The Miner and the Blacksmith post mining jobs. Mine the asked number of ore blocks yourself, in any kind of rock, then report back. You keep all the ore you dig. Ore broken in Creative mode does not count. Raid A group of hostiles spawns on the outskirts of town and marches toward your borders. Kill every mob in the group to complete the contract. Map markers and a raid health bar show which enemies count toward the quest. Now and then the board posts a harder contract: a very large delivery order, or an elite raid with more enemies and stronger leaders. These give a week to finish, pay well in gold, and are the contracts that reward Shards of Gaia and Verdant Catalysts . Every town rank has at least one. Every town rank has at least two different raids, and new ones appear as the town ranks up: goblin scouts and vermin at first, then undead, trorks, voidspawn, outlanders, scaraks and finally whole armies. From rank D upward most raids are led by tougher leaders , such as a trork chieftain or a goblin feastmaster. Harder raids bring more enemies and pay more gold and a bigger bundle of materials that suits the enemy. Rank and rewards Each completed board quest grants rank XP for your town. Higher town rank unlocks tougher tiers with better payouts. Cards show a time limit in days — finish before it expires or the slot clears at dawn. Rewards include gold, items, and reputation with the posting villager when the quest grants it. Tracking Active board quests appear on the Quests tab of your town journal alongside story quests. You can abandon a board quest from the journal if you change your mind. See Guild hall and guards under Mechanics for how to build the hall where the board lives.

name: Reputation
description: Friendship, gifts, and milestone rewards
text: Reputation Reputation is how much a villager trusts and likes you. It is personal: your score with the farmer does not change your score with the merchant. The meter runs from 0 to 100. Higher reputation unlocks milestone rewards and sometimes new recipes. Milestone progress and gift taste spoilers for each character are in the Villagers tab of your town journal. Gift history is on the town records shelf in the inn or town hall. Ways to raise reputation Talk each day The first time you speak with a villager after a new morning, you earn a small reputation bonus. Stop by while you are already walking the town. It adds up over time. Give gifts During dialogue, choose the gift option while holding an item in your hand. The villager reacts based on whether they love, like, feel neutral about, or dislike the gift. Better reactions give more reputation. A gift they dislike can lower it. You can only give so many gifts per villager per week, so save strong gifts for people you are trying to impress. A Wintertide gift to a villager counts twice as much toward friendship. When your friendship with a villager is full, they remember your birthday . They walk up and give you a present, the same kind they would bring on Wintertide. Complete quests Story quests from the Elder, innkeeper, and other residents often grant reputation when you finish them. The Quests tab in your journal shows item rewards and reputation lines when a quest grants them. Milestone rewards Each villager has their own friendship milestones at set reputation levels (not every character uses the same steps). When you cross a threshold, a reward waits for you. Talk to that villager to receive it. Rewards can be items, recipe knowledge, or a special thank-you conversation. If you pass several milestones at once, talk once and work through what they owe you. The Villagers tab in your journal lists each character and their milestones without spoiling every gift preference. Gift history on the town records shelf Open the town records shelf (inn or town hall) and browse by villager. You can see gifts you already gave and how they felt about each one. That helps you avoid repeating mistakes and plan the next present. Tips Rings and necklaces are on every town villager's liked gifts list. Jewelry is a reliable choice before you learn someone's personal favorites. Unidentified jewelry still counts once it is a real ring or necklace in your hand. Read Jewelry under Mechanics for finding and crafting pieces. Combine daily visits, quest lines, and thoughtful gifts on the villagers you care about most. Milestone rewards are claimed in person. If you crossed a threshold and nothing happened, find them in the world and start dialogue.

name: Spirit Garden
description: Grow renewable potion plants and petals in Spirit Planters
text: Spirit Garden Recruit Rowan Mossweald , build his Conservatory and finish the recruitment quest. He gives you two Spirit Planters. Rowan grows the town's potion plants in Spirit Planters . Craft more at the Town Planning Desk from wood, Life Essence and soil. 1. Place a Spirit Planter anywhere inside your town. Leave two free blocks above it. 2. Use the planter and pick one of the seeds you carry. It takes one seed. 3. Rowan does the rest during his work hours. He plants the seed, grows it with his rite, gathers the harvest and carries it to the Conservatory. A plant needs three rites to ripen, and it rests for a few hours between them. Rowan must stand at the planter for each rite, so the garden only grows while he is on shift and someone from town is nearby. After each harvest the plant starts again in the same planter for free. Each harvest brings plants and their petals to the Conservatory's storage cupboard. Blood plants give Blood Petals, Storm plants give Storm Petals and Azure plants give Azure Petals, so the town can brew its own potions. Open the cupboard or any planter to see the whole garden, collect what is stored and uproot a plant you no longer want. Couriers can also carry stored plants and petals to your brewers. Rowan needs Mastery 1 for the first tier of Health, Stamina and Mana plants, 4 for the second and 7 for the third. He earns Mastery with every harvest he brings home, and you can train him with Verdant Catalysts through his Profile. The seed list on a new planter shows what he can grow now. If the stores are full of a plant and its petals, Rowan leaves that planter ripe until you make room. Breaking a planter frees it and removes its plant. Blessings and garden upgrades Bless a planter with 5 Life Essence to double its next harvest. Choose Garden upgrades on the Spirit Garden screen, or ask Rowan about upgrades. They are paid with Life Essence and the plants he grows, taken from your pack first, then from the Conservatory's stores and the warehouse. - More planters lets Rowan tend up to six Spirit Planters. He starts with two. - Stronger rite shortens the rest between rites, so plants ripen sooner. - Bountiful harvest adds plants and petals to every harvest. - Wider stores lets the Conservatory hold more of everything. Seeds and older gardens Seed and sapling recipes are available at Crafting workplaces and use the Apprentice's Farming skill. Alchemical seed tiers need Farming 1, 4 and 7 . Check each recipe for its cost and equipment requirements. Ordinary seeds cost Life Essence and alchemical seeds cost Void Essence, both at the base game's rates. Plants you set on Crystal Soil by hand are ordinary plants. Rowan leaves them alone and you can harvest them yourself. Herb Garden workplaces have been removed. These plants produce potion ingredients. They do not provide town food support. If a planter is waiting Check its selected seed, two free blocks above it, Rowan's Mastery, access, work hours and storage room. A ripening rest between rites is normal. These are Rowan's core plants; enable Mycologist or Berry Patch priorities only for the separate Townsfolk workplaces.

name: Sprinklers
description: Water many farm cells at once
text: Sprinklers Sprinklers water many farm cells at once on the farm plot . They are unlocked through friendship with the Farmer . How they work Place a sprinkler on the farm plot like other farm equipment. At dawn each day, an placed sprinkler refreshes crops in its radius automatically. You can also use the block manually to trigger a watering pass outside the daily schedule. There are four tiers of sprinkler. Higher tiers cover a larger radius. Unlock tiers through the Farmer's friendship rewards and farm progression. Read Production wardrobe if you configure which crops the farm generates, and Villager needs to see why well-fed townsfolk pay more in the morning tithe.

name: Tourist portal
description: Daily visitors who shop and can move in
text: Tourist portal The tourist portal draws travelers from beyond your town borders. Lyren the Elder offers the build quest after the town hall is standing. Building the portal 1. Talk to Lyren and accept the tourist portal quest. 2. Take the tourist portal plot token from Lyren. 3. Stake and build the tourist portal prefab. 4. Find Lyren and close the quest in dialogue. Daily visits Each morning, tourists can arrive through the portal. They walk around town, browse shop spots (including your player shop), and leave at night . Tourists are hand-picked characters with personality traits that shape their dialogue. They are separate from inn visitors — see Inn pool and visitors under Mechanics for the inn's two-guest rotation. Inviting tourists to stay If you want a tourist to become a permanent resident, offer them a house : 1. Build a house plot and assign them on the management block through the appropriate housing quest flow. 2. Once registered, they count toward town life like other residents. Tourists who shop at player listings spend real gold from their pockets — a good reason to stock your shop spots with useful goods. Tips Finish Your Own Shop (from Vex) before expecting much tourist spending — they buy from player shop spots. The portal and inn serve different roles: the inn locks story visitors for quests; the portal brings repeat tourists each day.

name: Townsfolk stats and equipment
description: Attributes, profession skills, Mastery and training
text: Townsfolk stats and equipment Open a resident Townsfolk's Profile through dialogue or the Town Journal. Their abilities belong to that person and remain through resurrection. Attributes and profession skills The five attributes are Strength, Intelligence, Vitality, Dexterity and Speed . Attributes affect combat and movement. Knights favor Strength, Archers and Rogues favor Dexterity, and Mages favor Intelligence. Vitality improves health. The twelve profession skills are Blacksmithing, Ranching, Farming, Mining, Building, Alchemy, Crafting, Leatherworking, Cooking, Logistics, Commerce and Jewelry . Skills run up to 10 . A skill at zero is unavailable to that person and cannot be opened by normal training. Work types can share a skill while having separate priorities. Smelting, Blacksmithing and Armor Crafting all use Blacksmithing. Farming, Mycologist and Berry Patch use Farming. Crafting and Salvaging use Crafting. Read the selected task's skill requirement: seed recipes at a Crafting workplace use Farming. Earn and spend points Completed profession work earns personal Mastery XP, up to Mastery 20 . Each level gained gives one skill point . Levels 5, 10, 15 and 20 also give two attribute points . Spend them through the profile. One Verdant Catalyst raises an available profession skill by one; one Gaia Shard raises an attribute by one. Attributes cap at 20 . These training items do not raise Townsfolk Mastery itself. Named core specialists have their own Mastery system, described in Mastery and training . Townsfolk do not use their friendship or reputation rewards. Equip the right job Use the profile's equipment controls to choose compatible profession equipment. Delivery packs, farming tools, ranching equipment and crafting kits help their matching work. A Joiner's Toolbox improves Crafting and a Leatherworker's Roll improves Leatherworking. Equipment does not replace a required bench, unlock or skill. Guard kits use a separate equipment slot and apply to the matching class while on duty. A guard does no civilian profession work. Return them to civilian life before expecting workplace tasks. A high skill alone does not start work: the resident must be employed, paid, have the correct priority enabled and be able to reach an eligible task. See Work priorities and wages .

name: Town records shelf
description: Browse town info in the world
text: Town records shelf The Town Records Shelf brings together your building and town controls. The first tab shows the assigned worker. Use Teleport to me beside their name to bring them to you if they become stuck. Open the residents tab to browse both villagers and townsfolk , with portraits, page controls and filters. Select a resident for their needs, or choose Profile for their abilities, reputation and discovered gift preferences. Gifts and friendship rewards stay hidden until discovered or unlocked. Use the player management tab to invite members and change their town permissions. The move control lets you relocate the building. Remove anything you want to keep that was not part of its original design before moving it, including animals. Block palettes Open the paintbrush tab on a finished building to change its walls, roofs, wood, stone, cloth, and more. Use a Block Palette item to unlock looks for your town, then cycle each type to a look you have (or Default for the original) and hit Save. Your choices stay when you repair, rebuild, or move the building. Building upgrades Open Building upgrades through the building's villager or production controls. Warehouse storage also has a Building upgrades button. Select a node to see its benefit, Town Level, earlier upgrades and costs. Grey nodes with padlocks are locked. A node stands out when its prerequisites are satisfied. Production storage upgrades remain with the plot when you move or reconstruct the building. Warehouse storage expansions belong to the town.

name: Treasury and taxes
description: Gold flow for the town
text: Treasury and taxes The treasury block inside the town hall holds your town's gold coins. You need the hall built before you can deposit, withdraw, and read tax lines in one place. Morning tithe Each morning, villagers who count as residents pay a tithe based on how comfortable they are. Comfortable means their hunger , energy , and fun meters are in good shape. See Villager needs for how to keep those filled. Tax collection runs while at least one member of your town is online . Gold still accrues for unloaded town chunks, but no tithe runs while every town member is offline . Open the treasury UI to see coins add up. The second tab shows a breakdown of who paid what. Wage bills Employed Apprentices earn weekly wages. Open Bills in the treasury or Town Journal to see unpaid wages and their deadlines. Pay them from treasury funds. A paid bill leaves the list; an overdue bill pauses that worker until it is settled. The Work page lets you change employment, priorities and guard duty. Increasing income Several town systems raise how much you earn beyond the base tithe, including: Feasts and feast policies The founder statue Other town policies shown in treasury menus Read Getting Started for when Lyren asks you to raise the town hall, and Inn pool and visitors for guests who are not full residents.

name: Villager needs
description: Hunger, energy, fun, and where villagers go
text: Villager needs Every villager in town tracks three needs: hunger , energy , and fun . Each meter runs from empty to full. You can see them on the town records shelf in the inn or town hall, under the Needs tab. Villagers show how they feel through gestures, sounds, and thought bubbles. A hungry villager may hold their stomach and think about food. Tired villagers yawn, and bored villagers sigh or look around for company. Why needs matter Villagers slowly get hungrier, tire out, and want entertainment as the day goes on. When a meter is low, they look for the right place in town to fix it. Needs also tie into taxes . Each morning, residents pay gold into the treasury. The amount depends partly on how comfortable they are. Comfortable villagers pay more. Keeping meters up is good for them and for your town wallet. Points of interest Finished buildings add spots villagers can use: beds, benches, counters, workbenches, and similar blocks. Think of each spot as a small action in the world. Beds refill energy only (including beds in houses at night). Benches and seats with a fun spot refill fun only, including park benches. Meal spots (inn hearth, restaurant chairs, counters, and food storage) refill hunger only. Workbenches and shop counters are for the job. They do not refill any need by themselves. Conversations refill fun for both villagers while they spend time together. Different plots place different spots. A farm has farming benches. An inn has beds and meal space. A park has outdoor benches meant for relaxing. How villagers pick a spot Villagers follow a daily schedule, but a very low meter can pull them away for a while. If hunger is critical, they head for food. If energy is low, they seek a bed. If fun is low, they look for a bench or social spot. You do not need to click each spot yourself. Build the right plots and they will find them as the day runs. Conversations and personalities When fun is low, villagers can seek out a nearby neighbor for a chat. They take turns talking, telling stories, asking questions, and reacting. They still visit parks, and they leave conversations when they need food or rest. Speech bubbles show what they are discussing. Thought bubbles show interests and feelings. A thrifty villager may think about gold, a bookworm about books, and a gardener about flowers. Named villagers can also think about their favorite gifts. Shared interests can bring happy reactions, while disliked gifts may earn a doubtful look. Houses at night A house is optional. Villagers only need their workplace plot to hold a job in town. If you assign someone to a house, they can sleep there at night. That sleep refills energy , which keeps them comfortable for the next morning tithe. Use a park when fun is the problem. Tips If fun is always the lowest meter, stake a park plot from your planning desk. Park benches are built for relaxing. Use the records shelf Needs tab to see everyone at a glance and teleport a villager to you if you want to check on them. Feasts and some town policies can change how much gold you earn from comfortable residents. Read Treasury and taxes for the money side.

name: Warehouse and deliveries
description: General storage, crafted goods, building outputs and couriers
text: Warehouse and deliveries Recruit Mara Finch , available from Town Level 2, build her Warehouse and finish her recruitment quest. Use the Warehouse Ledger Desk to open town storage. Three kinds of storage - General storage holds supplies you deposit. Use search, switch between grid and list views, or use Store matching to deposit carried kinds already stored there. - Crafted Goods holds completed Apprentice crafting orders. Collect finished equipment, meals and building blocks here. Deposits belong in General storage. - Building Outputs shows resources kept by core production buildings and workplaces with their own stores, including mineshafts, mushrooms and berries. These items remain at their original source and retain that source's capacity. Collecting output makes room for more work. Seeing goods in Building Outputs does not move them into General storage or increase their capacity. Collect barn milk with empty buckets. Set up deliveries 1. Employ a civilian Townsfolk with nonzero Logistics skill. 2. Enable Logistics on the journal's Work page and keep their wages paid. No Logistics workplace or bench is needed. 3. Queue a workplace task and put the required supplies in town storage or an eligible production source. Keep the ledger desk, workplace and source accessible. Couriers reserve supplies, collect them and deliver them where needed. Each material is fetched from a source with enough available stock. If that stock changes before pickup, the delivery is planned again. Reserved stock cannot also be spent on another task. A full destination pauses delivery. Crafting workplaces can receive several crafts' ingredients per trip. Food workplaces provide population support rather than goods for delivery. Read Logistics and couriers for troubleshooting. More room and remote access Use Building upgrades to see storage expansions, their Town Level and treasury costs. Deep shelves increases stacks per slot in General storage; it does not enlarge every production building's stores. Mara's friendship unlocks a Warehouse Supply Link recipe, a Quartermaster Pack recipe and a Field Ledger . A Supply Link near ordinary workbenches makes eligible town supplies available for player crafting while respecting reservations. The Field Ledger opens storage while you are inside town. The Quartermaster Pack is Townsfolk profession equipment, separate from your portable backpack.

name: Work priorities and wages
description: Employ Townsfolk, choose their jobs and keep wages paid
text: Work priorities and wages The journal's Work page controls civilian Townsfolk. Core specialists such as Irienne and Seren follow their own work systems. Start a worker 1. Invite a Townsfolk to settle and make sure your town has room for them. 2. Employ them on the Work page. 3. Enable a profession they can do. 1 is highest priority ; a dot disables that work type. A zero skill means they cannot do that profession. 4. Provide a ready workplace and task, or an eligible Logistics delivery or Commerce assignment. 5. Keep their wages paid and the walking route clear. Priorities choose among available jobs. Setting Farming to 1 cannot make a site with a missing bench or unusable growing space ready. A worker with every other priority disabled may wait when that one job has no work due. Farming care, for example, is periodic. Workplace types that share a skill still have separate priorities. Enable Armor Crafting for armor orders, Block Workshop for crafted building blocks, and Mycologist or Berry Patch for those growers. Wages and availability Review weekly wages in Bills in the journal or treasury. Pay from treasury funds before the deadline. An overdue worker stops until their bill is paid; changing priorities does not change their wage. Guards do no profession work on duty. Use Guard: Off or the profile's return-to-civilian option when permitted. Residents also break for needs, and they need reachable work in active terrain. Wages and Apprentice work pause while no town member is in the town's world. Food-workplace neglect also pauses during that absence. The town does not keep distant work areas loaded. Waiting for work Open the workplace first and read its specific status. Check the type unlock, required bench and tier, marked floor and height, ingredients or fuel, output room, required skill and task order. Then check employment, priority, wages, guard duty and access. Logistics needs deliveries to make, not a marked workplace. Commerce needs a player-shop clerk assignment. Their individual pages explain setup.

name: Villagers
description: Who lives in town, what they need from you, and how to befriend them
text: Villagers Each resident has a dedicated page with quests , friendship rewards , and a weekly routine pulled from their in-game schedule. Villagers join town life in two ways: a workplace on their job plot (required for them to work there), and an optional house plot where they can sleep at night. See Getting Started for the difference between guests, visitors, and full residents. Open a name on the left for quest steps and where to find that villager during the day. For gift preferences while playing, the in-game journal can hide spoiler lists until you choose to show them. Every core villager offers a home quest after their work-building recruitment quest . Build a house, assign that villager on its Town Records Shelf and return to finish the quest. This includes the new specialist residents. Open a villager's Profile for their portrait, reputation and discovered gift preferences. Locked reputation rewards stay hidden until you unlock them. Core workers show one segment per Mastery level. Townsfolk have no reputation or friendship rewards. Their profiles show profession skills, attributes and equipment. They earn Mastery XP through completed work, receive a skill point each level and two attribute points every five levels.

name: Orin Glasswick
description: Discover mixtures and improve your reusable Alchemy Flask
text: Orin Glasswick becomes available at the Inn at Town Level 5 . Complete his Laboratory and return to him to finish his recruitment quest. The Laboratory is available in the Core style. Open Alchemy and flasks under Mechanics for the complete brewing guide, or Alchemy workplace for queued Townsfolk recipes. Your first flask Use the large cauldron inside the completed Laboratory and choose Craft flask . A flask costs 5 Iron Ingots, 5 Light Leather and 5 Tree Sap, taken from your inventory first and then from town storage. There is no recipe to learn. A new flask is empty and holds one charge. Bring the flask and ingredients to the large cauldron inside the completed Laboratory. Choose an available ingredient from your inventory or town storage. Fill flask bottles the mixture at once as a Good potion. Hold the brew steady For a better potion, choose Start brewing first. A brew lasts 10 beats, and each press of a button is one beat. The heat rises by itself every beat. Stoke raises it faster and Stir cools it. A glowing band drifts along the heat gauge, and a beat counts when the heat marker ends inside it. The small arrows show where each choice would put the heat, and the pale outline shows where the band is heading. - Good, five or fewer beats in the band: the listed duration and restoration. - Great, six to eight beats: lasting effects run 25% longer; Health, Mana and Stamina restoration increases by 10%. - Perfect, nine or ten beats: lasting effects run 50% longer; restoration increases by 20%. Nothing is spent until you fill a flask, so you can brew again as often as you like, and you can stop and bottle a Good potion at any moment. Each extra ingredient in the mixture makes the band narrower and quicker. Orin's Mastery makes it wider. The quality stays with the potion until the flask is empty and is shown on the flask. Changing ingredients starts a new brew. Bottling discovers the selected ingredients' properties for your town. Health, Mana and Stamina plants restore those resources, with stronger plant tiers giving stronger effects. Some mushrooms provide temporary protection or increase maximum health or mana. Explore their properties at the cauldron. When two ingredients give the same kind of effect, only the stronger effect applies. Wild flowers are worth trying too. Blue Aloe and green mushrooms heal you slowly over time, with rarer green mushrooms healing more. A Fire Flower keeps fire and lava from harming you for a short while. Lavender and Chrysanthemum make a bug repellent, so scaraks, spiders and scorpions leave you alone until you attack one. The Florist sometimes stocks these flowers. Each drink consumes one saved charge. An empty flask can be filled again. To replace a mixture before it runs out, choose Empty flask at the cauldron; its remaining potion is lost. If you carry several flasks, use Next to choose one. Laboratory upgrades The cauldron begins with one ingredient slot. Open Building upgrades to buy a second slot with Alchemist Mastery 3 and 150 treasury gold , then a third with Mastery 6 and 350 treasury gold . These let you combine different effects in one mixture. Orin earns Mastery XP when you bottle mixtures. You can also train him through his Profile, where each Verdant Catalyst adds one level. Flask capacity Upgrade the selected flask at the cauldron. Each purchase adds one maximum charge and keeps the potion already inside. It does not refill the flask. - Two charges: Alchemist Mastery 2 and 5 Light Leather. - Three charges: Mastery 4 and 10 Medium Leather. - Four charges: Mastery 6 and 15 Heavy Leather. - Five charges: Mastery 8 and 20 Storm Leather. Filling a flask consumes one of each selected ingredient per charge . A five charge flask with three ingredients therefore needs five of each ingredient. The cauldron spends them only when the flask is filled. Apprentice brewing Orin also supervises Alchemy workplaces. Unlock Alchemy through his workplace controls, mark a site with the Building Sta

name: Tobin Reedwright
description: Prop patterns and Crafting workplaces
text: Tobin can visit from Town Level 3 . Complete his Artisan Workshop , then unlock Crafting workplaces through his dialogue. Mark a workplace with the Building Staff and place an ordinary Workbench inside it. Employ an Apprentice, enable Crafting on the journal's Work page, and add orders through the workplace controls. The recipe list includes recipes registered for the ordinary workbench, including recipes supplied by other packs. Each recipe keeps its materials and bench requirements. Seed and sapling plans use Life Essence and the Apprentice's Farming skill. Alchemical seeds use Void Essence , exactly as at the Alchemy Bench. The task screen shows the required Farming level for each plant. Couriers bring ingredients, and completed crafting orders go to Crafted Goods . Bench upgrades and required recipe unlocks still apply. A Pattern Cabinet improves attended Crafting work speed without replacing the workbench. Open Crafting workplace and Salvaging workplace for Apprentice setup. Tobin's Pattern Book under Mechanics is the dedicated guide to his prop service. Tobin's Pattern Book Tobin can build any prop he has studied. Talk to him and choose Open your Pattern Book . 1. Show him a prop. Carry any prop and choose Show Tobin the props you carry . He sketches every new one into his book and hands them all back. The whole town shares his book. 2. Commission a copy. Pick a known pattern and choose Commission one . Props cost simple materials, never gold. 3. Collect it. Tobin builds the first prop on his bench during his work hours. Finished props wait on his shelf. Props Tobin has not seen yet show as a question mark. Cap'n Clive, treasure, gifts and festivals are good places to find new ones. Materials Every prop is made from four ordinary resources. Tobin takes them from your pack first, then from the town warehouse. - Sticks - Stone Rubble - Scraps - Linen Scraps Gather them as usual, or have Apprentices make them at a Crafting workplace. Their task list includes all four: 5 of any wood makes 10 Sticks, 5 of any stone makes 10 Stone Rubble, 5 of any metal bar makes 10 Scraps, and 10 fibre makes 5 Linen Scraps. The Logger's grove also brings home sticks with every tree, and goblins carry Scraps. A more valuable prop needs more materials and more time. The kinds it needs follow what it is made of. A plank shelf asks for Sticks and a weapon rack asks mostly for Scraps. Salvage Pick a prop you carry and choose Salvage one to have Tobin take it apart. You get half of its materials back, and he learns its pattern if he did not know it. Cancelling a commission returns everything. Collection goals - 5 patterns: a third commission on the bench. - 10 patterns: salvaging returns three quarters of the materials. - 20 patterns: a fourth commission on the bench. - 30 patterns: commissions take a quarter less time. name: Elara Willowmere
description: Clinic supplies and recovery for injured residents.
text: Elara Willowmere becomes available at the Inn at Town Level 4 . Build her Clinic to give your residents a place to recover. Open Clinic and recovery under Mechanics for setup and treatment troubleshooting. Clinic care Talk to Elara and choose Let us check the clinic . The medicine cabinet accepts Lesser Health Potions from your inventory. Each bottle supplies 80 medicine , and the cabinet holds 800 . Medicine is spent only when someone receives healing. Bring injured guards into the clinic with Follow , then ask them to Wait Here . Elara treats one nearby resident at a time, seeing the most seriously injured first. Both people must remain inside the clinic and close together. Twelve quiet seconds restore up to forty health. Fighting and new injuries interrupt treatment. Elara also needs to take breaks for food and rest. The clinic cannot revive the dead. Visit the Gaia Altar for revival. Guards also recover slowly when resting safely. After thirty quiet seconds, they recover a little health every ten seconds. Clinic medicine provides faster recovery. The care screen shows Elara's availability and treatment progress while it is open. Friendship Elara offers care packages at 25, 50 and 75 reputation. The first helps stock the clinic; later packages contain stronger potions for your journeys.

name: Rowan Mossweald
description: Grow alchemical plants and petals in the Spirit Garden
text: Rowan Mossweald becomes available at the Inn at Town Level 4 . Build his Conservatory and return to him to complete his recruitment quest. He gives you two Spirit Planters when it is finished. Open Spirit Garden under Production buildings for setup and troubleshooting. Rowan also supervises the Mycologist and Berry Patch workplace types. The Spirit Garden Rowan grows the town's potion plants in Spirit Planters . Craft more at the Town Planning Desk from wood, Life Essence and soil. 1. Place a Spirit Planter anywhere inside your town. Leave two free blocks above it. 2. Use the planter and pick one of the seeds you carry. It takes one seed. 3. Rowan does the rest during his work hours. He plants the seed, grows it with his rite, gathers the harvest and carries it to the Conservatory. A plant needs three rites to ripen, and it rests for a few hours between them. Rowan must stand at the planter for each rite, so the garden only grows while he is on shift and someone from town is nearby. After each harvest the plant starts again in the same planter for free. Each harvest brings plants and their petals to the Conservatory's storage cupboard. Blood plants give Blood Petals, Storm plants give Storm Petals and Azure plants give Azure Petals, so the town can brew its own potions. Open the cupboard or any planter to see the whole garden, collect what is stored and uproot a plant you no longer want. Couriers can also carry stored plants and petals to your brewers. Rowan needs Mastery 1 for the first tier of Health, Stamina and Mana plants, 4 for the second and 7 for the third. He earns Mastery with every harvest he brings home, and you can train him with Verdant Catalysts through his Profile. The seed list on a new planter shows what he can grow now. If the stores are full of a plant and its petals, Rowan leaves that planter ripe until you make room. Breaking a planter frees it and removes its plant. Blessings and garden upgrades Bless a planter with 5 Life Essence to double its next harvest. Choose Garden upgrades on the Spirit Garden screen, or ask Rowan about upgrades. They are paid with Life Essence and the plants he grows, taken from your pack first, then from the Conservatory's stores and the warehouse. - More planters lets Rowan tend up to six Spirit Planters. He starts with two. - Stronger rite shortens the rest between rites, so plants ripen sooner. - Bountiful harvest adds plants and petals to every harvest. - Wider stores lets the Conservatory hold more of everything. Seeds and older gardens Seed and sapling recipes are available at Crafting workplaces and use the Apprentice's Farming skill. Alchemical seed tiers need Farming 1, 4 and 7 . Check each recipe for its cost and equipment requirements. Ordinary seeds cost Life Essence and alchemical seeds cost Void Essence, both at the base game's rates. Plants you set on Crystal Soil by hand are ordinary plants. Rowan leaves them alone and you can harvest them yourself. Herb Garden workplaces have been removed. These plants produce potion ingredients. They do not provide town food support. Friendship rewards - Friendship 25: Botanist's Tool Roll recipe for town blacksmithing. - Friendship 75: Verdant Catalyst recipe.

description: Quests, friendship, schedule, and gifts for Irienne Mossmark.
text: Irienne Mossmark is usually found at the farm plot when they are on shift. Quests Irienne's farm plot Give Irienne fenced ground and a bench so she can stop dreaming of rows on an inn floor. 1. Take the farm plot token from Irienne. 2. Stake and build the farm plot prefab. 3. Find Irienne at the farming bench and close the quest in dialogue. Irienne's home Irienne wants roots under rafters that belong to her, not borrowed floorboards by the kettle. 1. Take the house plot token from Irienne. 2. Place and build the house prefab. 3. Assign Irienne as resident on the house management block. 4. Find Irienne and close the quest in dialogue. For a dedicated setup guide, open Farm and Scarecrow Fields under Production buildings. For population support from Townsfolk, open Farming workplace . Irienne's Wheat for the Town quest teaches that separate workplace setup. The Scarecrow Fields Irienne works the town's crops from a crop plan . You paint which crop goes where. She tills the ground, sows from the farm's seed store, waters, harvests and sows again, all by herself during her work hours while someone from town is nearby. 1. Use the farm's storage cupboard to open the field planner directly, or place a Farmer's Scarecrow on open ground anywhere in town and use it. Irienne gives you one Scarecrow when her farm is built, and more are crafted at the Town Planning Desk . 2. Pick a crop in the palette and select cells on the map. Double click a cell to paint its whole bed. Right click a cell to clear it. Fill field paints everything that is free. 3. That is all. Until you paint a plan a farm keeps its old automatic production. The first painted cell hands the farm to Irienne. The farm building has a field of its own. Every Scarecrow claims the ground around it as one more field with its own plan. Cells that cannot be farmed are dark on the map, and hovering over one says why. Seeds. A farm starts with a handful of wheat and lettuce seeds. Each cell uses one seed when it is sown, and a harvest gives its seed back about half the time. When the seed store runs out Irienne makes seeds from the Life Essence in the farm's stores, at the price of the game's own Farming Bench. Add seeds moves the seeds you carry into the store. Soil. Every cell is Worn, Good or Rich, shown by its colour on the map. - Good soil is ordinary soil. - Rich soil doubles every harvest and has a small chance of a Golden Harvest , which every villager loves as a gift and which sells for a high price. - Worn soil will not hold water, so crops grow slowly there. Growing the same crop in a cell six times running wears it one step. Sowing a different crop than last time lifts it one step, so Rotate crops once a day keeps most of a field Rich. Compost mends Worn soil. Compost. The farm keeps 25 of each crop. Crops beyond that are not wasted: three spare crops make one compost, and Irienne spreads it on Worn soil. The Almanac. Each week the Almanac favours a few of the crops Irienne can grow. A favoured crop is planted already sprouted and gives one extra crop at every harvest. The Almanac button shows this week and the next. Farm upgrades are paid with Life Essence and crops, from your pack first, then from the farm's stores and the warehouse. - More Scarecrows lets Irienne tend up to three Scarecrow fields. She starts with one. - Wider reach makes every Scarecrow field larger. - Better watering wets the cells around the one she waters. - Seed saving makes every harvest give its seed back. - Richer compost needs fewer crops, and at its second level makes Good soil Rich. - Almanac insight favours a third crop each week, then shows a whole season ahead. Each crop needs the Farmer's Mastery and unlocks shown in the palette. Collect harvests from the field planner's stores or the warehouse's Building Outputs; the farm no longer opens a separate Building Output screen. She starts with a Crude Hatchet. Each timber's requirement follows its sapling's Farming Bench tier. Tier 4 needs Iron, tiers 5 and 6 need Thorium or Cobalt, and tiers 7 and above need Adamantite. Higher tools satisfy lower requirements. Each Rootstone tells you when Seren needs more Mastery or a better tool for its tree. See Mastery and training for the full progression. The Singing Grove Seren grows the town's wood on Rootstones . She gives you two when her lumbermill is finished. Craft more at the Town Planning Desk from stone, Life Essence and fibre. 1. Place a Rootstone on open ground anywhere inside your town. 2. Use the Rootstone and pick one of the saplings you carry. It takes one sapling. 3. Seren does the rest during her work hours. She plants the tree, sings it tall, fells it and carries everything back to the lumbermill. The stone then grows the same tree again for free, for as long as you leave it there. Any of 32 trees works once you own its sapling. A tree needs open space above and around its Rootstone. If there is not enough room, the Rootstone tells you what is in the way. Trees from different Rootstones cannot grow into each other, so give large trees plenty of space. Seren can tend two Rootstones at first. Lumbermill upgrades let her tend up to six, sing faster and store more. Open the lumbermill's stores, or any Rootstone, to see every stone at a glance. From there you can also: - Bless a Rootstone. Spend 5 Life Essence and its next tree gives double wood. - Uproot a tree. This frees the Rootstone so you can choose another tree or move the stone. A tree that is already standing stays where it is and becomes yours to chop. A stone that has not been planted yet returns its sapling. - Collect all. Take everything in the mill stores. You are free to trim or build around a grove tree. Seren simply harvests what is left of it. Breaking a Rootstone frees it in the same way as uprooting. A lumbermill that worked the old way keeps doing so until its first Rootstone is given a sapling. From then on Seren works the grove instead, and that cannot be undone. description: Quests, friendship, schedule, and gifts for Gorruk Stonevein.
text: Gorruk Stonevein is usually found at the miner's hut when they are on shift. Open Miner's Hut and mining nodes for core production, or Mining workplace for Townsfolk tunnels. Mastery and tools Gorruk's own production requires both his Mastery and an equipped Pickaxe. Talk to him to train Mastery with Verdant Catalysts and equip a better tool from your inventory. He starts with a Crude Pickaxe. Iron needs Mastery 3 and Copper; Thorium and Cobalt need Mastery 5 and 6 respectively and Iron; Adamantite needs Mastery 8 and Thorium or Cobalt. Higher tools satisfy lower requirements. See Mastery and training for the full table. These requirements are separate from the Mining skill used by Apprentices below. Apprentice mineshafts Unlock Mining through the Miner's upgrades. Use the Building Staff's Create workplace mode to mark a base area around a regular Workbench , then choose Mining and save. Use that Workbench to open the Mineshaft planner whenever you need it. The staff's Manage mineshafts mode also opens existing mines. Each map square covers 3 by 3 blocks. The planner shows your base in blue and saved passages in green. Click a base cell near the rock to choose the entrance. Set North, East, South or West, a length from 3 to 30 in steps of 3 blocks, and Level tunnel, Stairs up, Stairs down or Room. Rooms are 9 by 9 blocks and five blocks high. The gold cells preview the draft on the selected floor. Choose Review terrain , then Add reviewed tunnel to authorize digging. Draft changes do not replace existing orders. To extend a mine, click an existing passage and add another tunnel from it. Branches wait until their connecting tunnel is dug and its carried load is deposited at the base. Stair icons mark both the upward and downward connections on each floor. Use Floor up and Floor down to inspect each walking height. New stairs span seven blocks vertically and need at least nine blocks of length. Plan another stair segment from the end to reach further floors. The map direction controls pan the view. Base floor brings you home. Enable Mining for an employed, paid townsfolk in the journal. Workers excavate real terrain and carry up to 25 items at Mining 1, plus 10 for each additional Mining level. Higher skilled available apprentices get first choice of work. A miner keeps a partial bag when continuing into another ready tunnel at the same base. They deposit loads in the base workplace output, returning partial loads when work ends or is blocked. Choose Open output storage in the planner, or find the mine under Building Outputs in the Warehouse. Hover over Stored output for a quick summary. Keep the entrance and routes clear and the area nearby. Only the main workplace shows border particles. Couriers collect crafting supplies directly from each mine base. A core mine is not required. Renewable core Miner nodes are separate from these tunnels. Passages are three blocks wide and three high. Turn support beams, wall torches, ceiling lanterns and rails on or off separately before adding a route. Rails run along tunnels and stairs, but never rooms. Each one takes a single item: Hardwood - Beam , Crude Torch , Lantern or Rail . Posts, corners and ceiling pieces are all made from Hardwood - Beam. The planner shows how many the route needs and how many town storage holds. Put them in General storage at the Warehouse Ledger Desk . Miners take one for each piece they place, after the digging is done. Floor buttons switch between landings. Select a passage or the empty square just beyond its end to extend it at that height. Joined beam corners connect the posts to the ceiling supports. A tunnel can leave any landing or passage at that passage's height, in any direction except back under the stairs it starts from, and two tunnels may cross at the same height. Building plots, water, furnishings and protected terrain are excluded. The planner names what is in the way and where. Squares where stairs or a passage at another height go through the

description: Arena runs, creature unlocks and spoils
text: Kael can visit from Town Level 4 . Build his Hunter's Lodge and finish his recruitment quest. Open Hunter's Lodge and arena under Mechanics for setup, portal placement and troubleshooting. The arena The Hunt Beacon marks the centre of the arena. Keep a clear 9 by 9 floor around it with room overhead. The beacon must stay inside the completed lodge plot. Unlock creatures with treasury gold and samples of their drops. Choose Start to begin a run. Kael fights one creature at a time, collects its spoils and faces progressively stronger opponents. Runs never begin automatically and do not progress while the world is unattended. Skeletons provide bones and linen scraps. Goblin Scrappers provide Scraps, which Tobin uses for props. Frost undead also provide Ice Essence. Burnt and incandescent undead provide Cindercloth and Fire Essence. Outlanders provide Shadoweave. Void Crawlers and the larger Void Spawn provide Void Essence and can drop Voidhearts. Spoils follow the creature's normal drop chances and amounts, excluding weapons, armor and tools. Collected spoils stay safe when a run ends. Open the lodge's Production Storage to browse and collect spoils, or collect them through the town warehouse. Make space when the spoils racks fill. Couriers can use lodge supplies for workplace orders. When creating or editing a Hunter's Lodge, the creator and editor require both the Hunt Beacon and Production Storage inside its bounds. Select the beacon to see Hunt portal opens here , Creature entrance and Hunter's starting position markers. Their positions follow the building's orientation, not the beacon block's facing. Leave the whole 9 by 9 arena clear. Training Spend treasury gold on vitality, power, field dressing, Second Wind and larger spoils racks between runs. Training improves Kael's survival and lets him complete longer runs.

name: Thalen Meadowrun
description: Quests, friendship, schedule, and gifts for Thalen Meadowrun.
text: Thalen Meadowrun is usually found at the barn when they are on shift. For the complete setup and troubleshooting guide, open Barn and owned animals under Production buildings. Ranching workplace explains the separate food-support site for Townsfolk. Owned barn animals Choose Animal shop when speaking to Thalen to open his separate shop. Common animals cost 100 gold at Rancher Mastery 1, uncommon animals cost 250 gold at Mastery 4, and rare animals cost 500 gold at Mastery 7. Ask Thalen about Building upgrades to unlock more pens and improve the barn. Food is shown as a small corner badge on each animal portrait. Resource storage starts at 10 per resource and gains 10 with each storage upgrade. Existing excess stock stays available to collect. Your barn starts with one active pen. Building upgrades unlock up to five pens. Choose Choose on a pen to open a grid of animal cards showing their picture, name, hearts and preferred food. Select a card to assign that animal. Choosing an animal already in another pen swaps the two animals. Rest empties a pen without losing its animal. Animals keep their names and hearts while resting. Rename them from My animals . Animals stay at their marked pen and cannot be killed or captured. You do not need to bring wild animals, find a breeding pair or raise offspring. Building authors mark five animal pens in the building editor by clicking the floor where each animal should stand. Face the direction it should look. Use Adjust or remove on a marker to remove it. Older community barns without pen markers automatically look for clear floor spaces inside the barn. Each automatic pen needs a 3 by 3 floor with four clear blocks above it. The pen screen tells you when space is missing. Your animals and upgrades stay yours; updated building designs use their author's pen positions. Daily food and hearts Each active animal eats one serving of its own food each day, beginning at dawn. Choose Supply all in the Food bin to transfer as much of that food as fits, up to 64 servings per type. Couriers can also supply it from farm output and town storage. Automatic deliveries keep eight of each active food by default. Choose a different target or turn deliveries off using the courier button. You need a Warehouse Manager and a townsfolk worker with Logistics enabled. Common animals eat early crops: Chicken: Corn, Farming Bench tier 2 Pig: Turnip, tier 3 Rabbit: Carrot, tier 2 Sheep: Lettuce, tier 1 Goat: Cauliflower, tier 3 Uncommon animals eat later crops: Cow and Deer: Pumpkin, tier 4 Boar and Camel: Aubergine, tier 4 Tetrabird: Tomato, tier 5 Skrill: Chilli, tier 5 Rare animals need the latest vegetables or meat: Bear: Raw wildmeat Mosshorn: Onion, tier 7 Moose and Armadillo: Potato, tier 7 These tiers refer to the ordinary seed recipe at the Farming Bench. Wheat is not animal food. Feeding gives 20 affection. Use the interaction prompt on an animal to pet it for another 10 affection, once each day. Each 100 affection earns a heart, up to five hearts. Each heart adds 20% to resource yields over time. Naming, resting or moving an animal does not reset its daily care. Animal resources Active, fed animals produce all their resources every six hours of loaded game time. Production speed upgrades shorten this interval. Hearts increase yields. Chickens and Skrills give eggs. Cows give beef, medium hide and milk. Sheep give wildmeat, light hide and wool. Tetrabirds give wildmeat and dark feathers. Armadillos give wildmeat and sturdy chitin. Other animals give their normal meat and hide. All animals slowly produce poop. Open Resources to see each product's stored amount and capacity, including products that are still empty, and collect supplies. Bring an empty bucket for each milk bucket you collect. Full storage pauses the next resource bundle until there is enough room for every item. Animals that are resting, waiting for food or outside loaded chunks do not produce. Animal products never consume or kill an owned ani

name: Mara Finch
description: Town storage and courier deliveries
text: Mara can visit from Town Level 2 . Build her Warehouse and finish her recruitment quest. Open Warehouse and deliveries under Mechanics for the storage tabs, capacity upgrades, Supply Links and Field Ledger. Logistics and couriers explains the Townsfolk setup; no Logistics workplace is needed. Storage and deliveries Use the Warehouse Ledger Desk to open town storage. Search updates the item list while you type. General storage holds supplies, Crafted Goods holds finished workplace orders, and Building Outputs shows goods kept in each production source's own store. Locked choices explain their requirements. Use Store matching to deposit carried kinds already in General storage; production stores keep their own capacity limits. Enable Logistics for employed Townsfolk on the journal's Work page. Couriers carry reserved ingredients from storage and production buildings to workplaces. Completed crafting orders go to Crafted Goods . Supplies remain at their source until pickup. A full destination pauses the delivery. Each material is fetched from one place that holds enough of it: the production building or furnace that has it, otherwise general storage, which is collected at a ledger desk in the Warehouse. If that place is emptied before the courier arrives, the delivery is planned again. Choose Building upgrades from town storage to buy more storage room. Each expansion needs the previous expansion, the shown Town Level and treasury gold. Apprentice recipes only begin when the workplace has its bench, a qualified worker and the required supplies. Friendship rewards - Friendship 25: Warehouse Supply Link recipe. Craft it at the Town Planning Desk and place it within the normal chest range of your workbenches. It draws from general storage, crafted goods and building outputs, keeping courier reservations safe. Open the link to browse the warehouse. Collect barn milk into buckets first. - Friendship 50: Quartermaster Pack recipe. - Friendship 75: Field Ledger.

name: Welcome
description: Start here to learn Aetherhaven on the web and in your journal
text: Welcome to the guide This is the public Aetherhaven wiki at . The same articles appear in your in-game Town Journal while you play. Use the directory on the left to open a topic. Prefer the original English text? Open Town Journal → Settings → Personal and turn on Use English for Aetherhaven . It changes this mod's text and guide pages immediately, saves your choice for your character, and leaves your game's language alone. Turn it off to follow your game language again. Getting Started walks you through founding a town, your first buildings, and how money flows in. Mechanics explains tools, buildings, and systems you will use around town. Apprentice workplaces has its own section with setup and troubleshooting guides for every workplace, plus Logistics and Commerce. Villagers introduces each resident, their story quests, friendship rewards, and weekly routines. You can also browse Community Builds on the main site to download player-made plot prefabs for your town.

name: Alchemy workplace
description: What Alchemy does, its equipment and how to start work
text: Alchemy Apprentices brew queued potion recipes from plants, petals, mushrooms and other supplies. Set it up 1. Recruit the Alchemist , finish their work building and unlock Alchemy through their Apprentice workplace controls. You need a free workplace slot under that supervisor. 2. Use the Building Staff , choose Create workplace , and mark two opposite ground corners inside town. Choose Alchemy , name the area and save. Include the whole Alchemist's Workbench in its marked area and height. 3. Employ a civilian Townsfolk with a nonzero Alchemy skill. On the journal's Work page, enable Alchemy ; priority 1 is highest. Pay their wages and leave a clear walking route. Unlock Alchemy after Orin has settled in his Laboratory. Open the workplace's bench, choose a recipe, set its order mode and provide the ingredients through town storage. The Druid's Spirit Garden, Mycologist and Berry Patch can provide ingredients. Work and output Completed recipe items go to Crafted Goods . Employed Logistics workers deliver reserved supplies. The recipe screen shows missing ingredients, skill, equipment and town unlocks. If work is waiting This is Apprentice recipe work. To discover ingredient effects, play the heat minigame or refill a reusable flask yourself, read Alchemy and flasks and visit the Laboratory cauldron. Keep the area nearby and loaded. Workers also take breaks for their needs. Open Apprentice workplaces for shared staff controls, Work priorities and wages for employment, and Warehouse and deliveries for supplies.

Work and output Collect completed equipment from Crafted Goods or the task page. Equip a guard through their profile; making a kit does not equip it automatically. If work is waiting Enable Armor Crafting in priorities. It is separate from Blacksmithing even though both use the Blacksmithing skill. Check bench tier and recipe unlocks. Berries stay in the workplace store and can be collected there or through the warehouse's production view. Couriers can take them to kitchens. name: Commerce and shop clerks
description: Assign a Townsfolk to serve a player shop
text: Commerce and shop clerks A Commerce worker serves customers at a player shop during the day. Commerce uses its own skill and priority, with no Apprentice workplace area . Set it up 1. If the counter is unattended Check the shop assignment, employment, Commerce priority and guard duty. Clerks work during the day and still have needs. Other available jobs with higher priority can occupy them. Commerce does not produce Crafted Goods or add food-support points. Keep the shop stocked and use its own controls to manage sale items. Use the Building Staff , choose Create workplace , and mark two opposite ground corners inside town. Choose Farming , name the area and save. Include the whole Farmer's Workbench in its marked area and height. 3. Employ a civilian Townsfolk with a nonzero Farming skill. On the journal's Work page, enable Farming ; priority 1 is highest. Pay their wages and leave a clear walking route. Leave at least four clear dirt, grass or tilled-soil spaces at the marked floor with room above for wheat. Townsfolk prepare the ground and plant wheat themselves: you do not need seeds or existing crops. Keep the bench and growing spaces inside the marked bounds. Work and output Open Food support and tending to see the growing-space count and last care. Workers revisit every six game hours. After a full simulated day without tending, the food bonus pauses until care resumes. If work is waiting The screen identifies missing equipment, insufficient growing space, worker requirements and path problems. Selecting a crop or bench corner includes its base, but always review the marked floor and height. Irienne's Wheat for the Town quest walks through setup. For harvested items, use Farm and Scarecrow Fields instead. Keep the area nearby and loaded. Workers also take breaks for their needs. Open Apprentice workplaces for shared staff controls, Work priorities and wages for employment, and Warehouse and deliveries for supplies.

name: Logistics and couriers
description: Move supplies without creating a workplace
text: Logistics and couriers Logistics workers carry supplies between the warehouse, production sources and workplaces. This uses Logistics skill and needs no marked workplace or bench . Set it up 1. Recruit Mara Finch , finish her Warehouse and use the Warehouse Ledger Desk for town storage. 2. Employ a civilian Townsfolk with nonzero Logistics skill and enable Logistics on the journal's Work page. 3. Put materials in General storage , or make them available in the appropriate production store. 4. Queue work that needs them and keep a clear route between the source and destination. Couriers also supply supported construction projects and barn food requests. Set the barn's courier food target on its herd screen. Recipe supplies are reserved so two workers cannot spend the same stock. If deliveries are waiting Check available stock, not just the total shown: some may already be reserved. The source must have enough for the planned material, and both ends must have space and be reachable. Make sure the worker is paid and off guard duty. A Logistics worker can wait normally when nothing needs moving. Higher-priority ready work can also occupy them. Complete or cancel deliveries through their normal controls before removing a workplace, so carried materials can be returned. Warehouse and deliveries explains the storage tabs and capacity upgrades. Townsfolk stats and equipment explains profession packs.

name: Mining workplace
description: What Mining does, its equipment and how to start work
text: Mining Apprentices excavate real tunnels, stairs and rooms, then carry mined drops back to their base. Set it up 1. Recruit the Miner , finish their work building and unlock Mining through their Apprentice workplace controls. You need a free workplace slot under that supervisor. 2. Use the Building Staff , choose Create workplace , and mark two opposite ground corners inside town. Choose Mining , name the area and save. Include the whole Workbench in its marked area and height. 3. Employ a civilian Townsfolk with a nonzero Mining skill. On the journal's Work page, enable Mining ; priority 1 is highest. Pay their wages and leave a clear walking route. Use the Workbench to open the Mineshaft planner . Each map cell is three blocks wide. Select a blue base cell or a green passage, choose a direction and a length in three-block steps, then choose a level tunnel, stairs or a 9 by 9 room. Review terrain , then Add reviewed tunnel to authorize permanent digging. Work and output Enable Mining for an employed, paid townsfolk. A worker carries 25 items at Mining 1 and 10 more for each additional level. Collect from Open output storage in the planner or Building Outputs at the warehouse. A core mine is not required. If work is waiting Use floor controls to inspect connected passages. Seven-block stairs need at least nine blocks of length. Beams, torches, lanterns and rails need their named materials in General storage. Rails are not placed in rooms. Keep entrances clear and check terrain warnings and ore skill requirements. Removing an order does not restore dug terrain; remove connected branches first. Keep the area nearby and loaded. Workers also take breaks for their needs. Open Apprentice workplaces for shared staff controls, Work priorities and wages for employment, and Warehouse and deliveries for supplies.

name: Mycologist workplace

text: Mycologist Apprentices seed logs, tend growing mushrooms and harvest ingredients for cooking and Alchemy. Set it up 1. Use any log to open the growing screen and choose one mushroom type for the site. Check the chosen mushroom's Farming requirement. Work and output An Apprentice seeds each log, tends it twice as it grows and picks the harvest into the workplace's own store. Collect it there or through the warehouse's production view. Couriers can supply these mushrooms to recipes. If work is waiting Changing the mushroom clears every log, so finish the crop first if you want its harvest. A full store pauses work. Enable the Mycologist priority on a worker with enough Farming skill; enabling the Farming workplace priority alone is not the same job. Keep the area nearby and loaded. Workers also take breaks for their needs. Open Apprentice workplaces for shared staff controls, Work priorities and wages for employment, and Warehouse and deliveries for supplies.

name: Ranching workplace
description: What Ranching does, its equipment and how to start work
text: Ranching A tended Ranching workplace adds 10 food points , supporting five residents . It produces no inventory items . Set it up 1. Recruit the Rancher , finish their work building and unlock Ranching through their Apprentice workplace controls. You need a free workplace slot under that supervisor. 2. Use the Building Staff , choose Create workplace , and mark two opposite ground corners inside town. Choose Ranching , name the area and save. Include the whole Feeding Trough in its marked area and height. 3. Employ a civilian Townsfolk with a nonzero Ranching skill. On the journal's Work page, enable Ranching ; priority 1 is highest. Pay their wages and leave a clear walking route. Craft a Feeding Trough at a Workbench from 5 tree trunks and 10 Plant Fiber . Leave clear floor space around it inside the workplace. A cow and a chicken appear automatically; you do not need to bring animals or find a breeding pair. Work and output An employed worker with Ranching enabled tends the site. Open Food support and tending to check care and readiness. The food bonus pauses if the workplace is neglected for a full simulated day. If work is waiting Keep a clear route to the trough and space for both animals. Workplace animals stay nearby and cannot be captured or killed for resources. They disappear when the site is removed. The core Rancher's Barn and owned animals system has purchased animals, food and item output instead. Keep the area nearby and loaded. Workers also take breaks for their needs. If work is waiting Enable Salvaging , which is separate from Crafting in the priority grid even though it uses the Crafting skill. Check the order's accepted item, the worker's skill, deliveries and output capacity. Keep the area nearby and loaded. Workers also take breaks for their needs.
